## 4.13.153 P-0-1823.x.1, CCD: Default synchronization mode for axis n 

Allocation Contained in 18VRS: «-» «-» «-» «MPC» Contained in 20VRS: «-» «-» «-» «MPC» «-» Contained in 21VRS: «-» «-» «-» «MPC» «-» Hardware Controller A-CC -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: device-specific 

> Function This parameter defines a default synchronous operation mode for the IndraDrive axes. This is achieved by entering a characteristic number. 

The following settings can be selected: 

- Phase synchronization (0) 

- Cam (1) 

- MotionProfile (2) 

- Velocity synchronization (3) 

During initialization, the synchronization mode selected in parameter "P-0-1823.x.1" is set for the slave axis in parameter "P-0-0088, Control word synchronization modes". The setting made in this parameter is only required if bit "In Synchronization" is to be established in the slave axis before syn‐ chronization mode is activated with the correct operation mode. 

The structure index specifies the logic axis n for which the parameter takes effect.

> Function As of MPx-18VRS: "P-0-1808.2.31" replacement parameter for compatible access and for communication interfaces which do not support any 32-bit ident numbers (EIDN). 

In MLD system mode (P-0-1600), parameters "P-0-183x" are used for the re‐ al-time channel. 

"x" is the slave number → e.g., slave "1" 

See also Functional Description "Cross Communication (CCD)" 

> Use Observe the following aspects for use: 

- In CCD system mode and CCD basic mode, the parameters can be used as copy containers. 

- The data container can be used for transmission of 2 bytes data to the CCD slave in the command value telegram (e.g. P-0-1831 -> S-0-0080). 

Example: 

Slave 1 files "S-0-0084" to the AT -> Master copies to "P-0-1831" and files "P-0-1831" to the MDT for slave 1 as "S-0-0080". 

Parameters "P-0-1730" to "P-0-1809" are to be used for transmit‐ ting 4-byte data.

> Function As of MPx-18VRS: "P-0-1808.2.32" replacement parameter for compatible access and for communication interfaces which do not support any 32-bit ident numbers (EIDN). 

In MLD system mode (P-0-1600), parameters "P-0-184x" are used for the re‐ al-time channel. 

"x" is the slave number → e.g., slave "1" 

See also Functional Description "Cross Communication (CCD)" 

Observe the following aspects for use: 

- In CCD system mode and CCD basic mode, the parameters can be used as copy containers. 

- The data container can be used for transmission of 2 bytes data to the CCD slave in the command value telegram (e.g. P-0-1841 -> S-0-0080). 

Example: 

Slave 1 files "S-0-0084" to the AT -> Master copies to "P-0-1841" and files "P-0-1841" to the MDT for slave 1 as "S-0-0080". 

Parameters "P-0-1730" to "P-0-1809" are to be used for transmit‐ ting 4-byte data.

> Function As of MPx-18VRS: "P-0-1808.2.33" replacement parameter for compatible access and for communication interfaces which do not support any 32-bit ident numbers (EIDN). 

In MLD system mode (P-0-1600), parameters "P-0-185x" are used for the re‐ al-time channel. 

Bosch Rexroth AG R911328651_Edition 15 

IndraDrive MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB Parameters 

787/1717 

Product-specific parameters 

## "x" is the slave number → e.g., slave "1" 

See also Functional Description "Cross Communication (CCD)" 

Observe the following aspects for use: 

- In CCD system mode and CCD basic mode, the parameters can be used as copy containers. 

- The data container can be used for transmission of 2 bytes data to the CCD slave in the command value telegram (e.g. P-0-1851 -> S-0-0080). 

Example: 

Slave 1 files "S-0-0084" to the AT -> Master copies to "P-0-1851" and files "P-0-1851" to the MDT for slave 1 as "S-0-0080". 

Parameters "P-0-1730" to "P-0-1809" are to be used for transmit‐ ting 4-byte data.

In MLD system mode (P-0-1600), parameters "P-0-186x" are used for the re‐ al-time channel. 

"x" is the slave number → e.g., slave "1" 

See also Functional Description "Cross Communication (CCD)" 

Observe the following aspects for use: 

- In CCD system mode and CCD basic mode, the parameters can be used as copy containers. 

- The data container can be used for transmission of 2 bytes data from the CCD slave in the actual value telegram (e.g. P-0-1861 <- S-0-0084). 

Example: 

The slave files "S-0-0084" to the AT. The master copies the content of the AT to "P-0-1861". In the master, "P-0-1861" is used for internal processing 

Parameters "P-0-1730" to "P-0-1809" are to be used for transmit‐ ting 4-byte data.

> Function As of MPx-18VRS: "P-0-1808.2.51" replacement parameter for compatible access and for communication interfaces which do not support any 32-bit ident numbers (EIDN). 

In MLD system mode (P-0-1600), parameters "P-0-187x" are used for the re‐ al-time channel. 

"x" is the slave number → e.g., slave "1" 

See also Functional Description "Cross Communication (CCD)" 

Observe the following aspects for use: 

- In CCD system mode and CCD basic mode, the parameters can be used as copy containers. 

- The data container can be used for transmission of 2 bytes data from the CCD slave in the actual value telegram (e.g. P-0-1871 <- S-0-0084). 

- Example: 

The slave files "S-0-0084" to the AT. The master copies the content of the AT to "P-0-1871". In the master, "P-0-1871" is used for internal processing 

Parameters "P-0-1730" to "P-0-1809" are to be used for transmit‐ ting 4-byte data.

> Function As of MPx-18VRS: "P-0-1808.2.53" replacement parameter for compatible access and for communication interfaces which do not support any 32-bit ident numbers (EIDN). 

In MLD system mode (P-0-1600), parameters "P-0-189x" are used for the re‐ al-time channel. 

"x" is the slave number → e.g., slave "1" 

See also Functional Description "Cross Communication (CCD)" 

Observe the following aspects for use: 

- In CCD system mode and CCD basic mode, the parameters can be used as copy containers. 

- The data container can be used for transmission of 2 bytes data from the CCD slave in the actual value telegram (e.g. P-0-1891 <- S-0-0084). 

Example: 

The slave files "S-0-0084" to the AT. The master copies the content of the AT to "P-0-1891". In the master, "P-0-1891" is used for internal processing 

Parameters "P-0-1730" to "P-0-1809" are to be used for transmit‐ ting 4-byte data.

## 4.13.231 P-0-1901.0.1, CiA402: Controlword 

Allocation Contained in 20VRS: «MPB» «MPE» «-» «MPC» «-» Contained in 21VRS: «MPB» «-» «-» «MPC» «-» Hardware CiA402 -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: axis-specific 

Function 

The parameter realizes the object 0x6040 "Control word" for profile "CiA402". 

The description of the object can be found in specification "CiA 402 CANopen device profile for drives and motion control". 

Via parameter "P-0-1901.0.1" the Drive State Machine can be controlled in accordance with "CiA402". 

See also functional description "Profile types"

> Function The parameter realizes the object 0x6041 "status word" for the profile "CiA402". 

Parameter "P-0-1901.0.2" can be used to indicate the status of the drive state machine according to "CiA402". 

See also Functional Description "Profile types" 

Structure

|---|---|---|

|1|Switched on||
|2|Operation enabled||
|3|Fault||
|4|Voltage enabled||
|5|Quick stop||
|6|Switch on disabled||
|7|Warning||
|8/9|Reserved||
|10|Target reached||
|11|Internal limit active||
|12/13|Operation mode-specific||
|14/15|Reserved||

## 4.13.234 P-0-1901.0.4, CiA402: Quick stop option code 

> Function The parameter realizes object 0x605A "Quick stop option code" for profile "CiA402". 

Bosch Rexroth AG R911328651_Edition 15 

IndraDrive MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB Parameters 

807/1717 

Product-specific parameters 

Via parameter "P-0-1901.0.4" the deceleration ramp and reaction during the transition to the state “quick stop” of the drive state machine can be set in ac‐ cordance with "CiA402". 

- 0 = Disable drive function (torque enable) 

- 2 = Deceleration with 0x6085 "Quick stop deceleration" and subsequent transition to "Switch on disable" 

- 6 = Deceleration with 0x6085 "Quick stop deceleration" (S-0-0372) and maintaining in "Quick Stop" 

See also functional description "Profile types"

## 4.13.281 P-0-1901.0.67, CiA402:Positive torque limit value 

Bosch Rexroth AG R911328651_Edition 15 

IndraDrive MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB Parameters 

827/1717 

Product-specific parameters 

Structure 

This parameter allows a torque or force limit value to be determined for posi‐ tive torque/force command values. This limit value only takes effect with re‐ gard to the torque command value of the velocity controller (P-0-0049) and not with regard to the command values from the acceleration feedforward pa‐ rameters (S-0-0348, P-0-1126). 

During an error response, the limitation of the process torque of the "object 0x60E0" is not effective. The torque is limited by "P-0-0109". 

Positive torque takes effect in the case of: 

- Motive operation with positive velocity 

- Regenerative operation with negative velocity

> Function This parameter is used in conjunction with the enabling of functional pack‐ ages. 

In parameter "P-0-2002" the count of the operating hours counter of the con‐ trol section, at the time of a change in the functional package selection in "P-0-2003, Selection of functional packages", is stored. 

The value is stored on the control section and therefore gets lost when the device is replaced. Parameter P-0-2002 cannot be changed but only be read. 

See also Functional Description "Enabling of Functional Packages"

Use 

Observe the following aspects for parameterization: 

- When the mode is switched from parameterization mode (PM) to ope‐ rating mode (OM), this parameter is marked as invalid if enabled pack‐ ages were selected which may be active only alternatively in relation to each other. 

- Changes do not become effective before the drive is restarted the next time or "S-0-1350, C6400 Reboot command" is executed.

## 4.14.4 P-0-2051, Operating hours counter, motor 

Allocation 

|Contained in 16VRS:|«MPB»|«MPE»|«MPM»|||
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|Contained in 17VRS:|«MPB»|«MPE»|«MPM»|«MPC»||

|Contained in 20VRS:|«MPB»|«MPE»|«MPM»|«MPC»|«-»|
|Contained in 21VRS:|«MPB»|«-»|«MPM»|«MPC»|«-»|
|Hardware|--|||||
|Funct. package(s):|--|||||
|Device parameter:|axis-specific|||||



> Function This parameter displays the current count of the operating hours counter of the motor. 

The operating hours counter records the duration of three different operating states: 

- Motor enabled (AF, electric load) 

- Motor in motion (actual velocity unequal to "0") 

- Motor temperature less than 10 K away from "S-0-0204, Motor shut‐ down temperature" 

The following motor standstill thresholds take effect: 

- Rotary motor: 10 rpm 

- Linear motor: 10 mm/min 

Every hour the operating hours counter of the motor is saved and written to the encoder memory. If the 24V supply is interrupted within the 60 minutes, the parameter is not saved additionally. 

See Functional Description "Diagnostic data of motor operation"

|1|Motion duration|0.0|Time period during which the actual<br>velocity of the motor was unequal to<br>"0".|
|2|Motor warning tem‐<br>perature duration|0.0|Time period during which the motor<br>temperature had been less than 10K<br>below the switch-off threshold.|



Tab. 4-236: List elements of "P-0-2051, Operating hours counter, motor" 

## Use 

For motors without encoder data memory, the values of "P-0-2051" remain unchanged when switching to the operating mode (bb, Ab, OM). The time du‐ ration recording continues on the basis of the values of "P-0-2051" after the switchover to the operating mode if the respective time recording criterion is fulfilled. 

For motors with encoder data memory, the parameters P-0-2051, P-0-2052 and P-0-2053 cannot be written in parameterization mode (PM).

This parameter displays the current status of the thermal operating data: 

- Maximum temperature of motor 

- Average motor temperature during total operating time (motor in "AF") 

The values of the thermal operating data are only realistic, when the temperature sensor allows winding temperature measure‐ ment! This is impossible for temperature sensors with switching performance!

## 4.14.7 P-0-2054, Operational performance, motor 

Allocation 

- Function 

|Contained in 16VRS:|«MPB»|«MPE»|«MPM»|||
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|Contained in 17VRS:|«MPB»|«MPE»|«MPM»|«MPC»||

|Contained in 20VRS:|«MPB»|«MPE»|«MPM»|«MPC»|«-»|
|Contained in 21VRS:|«MPB»|«-»|«MPM»|«MPC»|«-»|
|Hardware|--|||||
|Funct. package(s):|--|||||
|Device parameter:|axis-specific|||||



To quantify the mechanical motion of the motor or the axis, the drive deter‐ mines the operational performance of the connected motor. For this purpose, a current value is generated in intervals of 8ms and added up. This value is calculated from the following product: 

- Current velocity (average absolute value over 8ms) 

- Duration of motor motion (rotary motor > 10min[-1] , linear motor >100mm/ min), max. 8ms 

The unit of the operational performance depends on the mechanical motor design (configured in P-0-4014): 

- Rotary motor: unit is 1000 rev 

- Linear motor: unit is meter 

The operational performance can be used as threshold value, e.g. for lubrication intervals. The user can reset or change the value. 

Replacing motors with diagnostic data in encoder memory (e.g. MSK, MS2N): 

- Changed motor serial numbers are recognized by the drive (comparison of "S-0-1300.20.12" (encoder memory) and "P-0-02055" (drive)) 

- The previous operational performance of the motor is saved in "P-0-2054" and calculated from the product of: 

   - P-0-3051, Encoder memory, operating hours counter, motor, "list element 1, motion duration", and 

   - P-0-3053, Encoder memory, mechanical operating data, motor, "list element 1, average velocity of motor in motion" 

The value of "P-0-2054" that is already available in the drive is overwritten with the operational performance value of the replace‐ ment motor without notification! 

Replacing MSM motors (encoder data memory can be used in a restricted way) 

- Value of "P-0-2054, Operational performance, motor" available in the drive parameter set is deleted, if "P-0-2055, Serial number, motor" in the drive did not contain any value. Furthermore, the serial number of the replacement motor in this case is applied to "P-0-2055"!

> Function This parameter serves for identification of the serial number and the connec‐ ted motor model. 

This functionality is only available for Rexroth motors with a QEM encoder data memory of version 4 (MSK) or 7 (MS2N). The serial number of the mo‐ tor serves for identification of the motor unit currently connected to the con‐ troller. This shows whether the motor connected to the controller was re‐ placed. Depending on the connected motor model, the operating data stored in the encoder is transferred to the controller or, if necessary, synchronized with the operating data available in the controller. 

See Functional Description "Diagnostic data of motor operation"

Parameter set switching is configured with this parameter. The parameter groups that are included in parameter set switching are defined and the switching behavior is parameterized. 

See also Functional Description "Parameter set switching" 

Structure 

The individual bits of the parameter have the following significances: 

|Bit|Designation/function|Comment|
|---|---|---|
|4-0|Parameter group selection<br>Bit 0: Group 1, application parameters<br>0:Cannot be switched<br>1:Can be switched<br>Bit 1: Group 2, control loop parameters<br>0:Cannot be switched<br>1:Can be switched<br>Bit 2: Group 3, load gear parameters<br>0:Cannot be switched<br>1:Can be switched<br>Bit 3: Group 4, winding parameters<br>0:Cannot be switched<br>1:Can be switched<br>Bit 4: Group 5, motor control and encoder parameters<br>0:Cannot be switched<br>1:Can be switched||
|7-5|Unassigned||
|8|Drive-controlled parameter set switching<br>0:Deactivated<br>1:Active||



Bosch Rexroth AG R911328651_Edition 15 

IndraDrive MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB Parameters 

845/1717 

Product-specific parameters 

|Bit|Designation/function|Comment|
|---|---|---|
|14-9|Unassigned||
|15|Position data reference in the case of gear switching<br>(encoder 1)<br>0:Is lost<br>1:Is maintained (S-0-0051jumps)|See note|



Tab. 4-239: Parameter set switching, group selection 

## Use 

Observe the following points when using the parameter: 

- It is possible to select none, multiple or all parameter groups for param‐ eter set switching. 

- The parameters which are combined in the respective group are descri‐ bed in chapter "Parameter set switching" of the Functional Description. 

- Which parameters are switched can be checked in parameter "S-0-0219, IDN-list of parameter set" after "P-0-2216" was changed. 

- If the gear ratio changes at gear switching, the exact reference position of encoder 1 cannot be guaranteed any more. This is signaled by the fact that its reference bit is cleared in "S-0-0403, Position feedback val‐ ue status". 

- If the gear ratio changes at gear switching, the position data reference is lost if the mounting position of the reference encoder does not comply with the selected data reference (e.g., data reference at load, reference via encoder 1/motor encoder). Hereby, the reference bit of the reference encoder is cleared in "S-0-0403, Position feedback value status". 

- Some controls no longer allow motion if "S-0-0403 = 0". To move the ax‐ is nevertheless, it is possible to keep the reference bits from being cleared by activating "maintain position data reference", although the position data reference of encoder 1 got lost. 

The position data reference is only safely reestablished, when a new homing procedure was executed! The reference of a spindle encoder (encoder 2) is maintained in the case of gear switching, if there is data reference to the load!

> Function This parameter can be used to enter a waiting time for defined delay of pa‐ rameter set switching. 

See also Functional Description "Parameter Set Switching" 

Use 

The parameter set switching functions is included in the base package of MPE. 

Observe the following aspects for using the parameter: 

- The waiting time is only effective if the "winding parameters" or "encoder parameters" parameter group is active. 

- The waiting time allows the user to wait until the motor contactors has been switched successfully in case of winding or encoder switching. 

- If the "winding parameters" parameter group is active, reactivation of drive enable is delayed; if the "encoder parameters" parameter group is active, the internal start of command C02 is delayed.

The parameter lists 

- P-0-2300, List of 32-bit IDNs and 

- P-0-2301, List of 16-bit alias IDNs 

allow converting 32-bit EIDNs to 16-bit alias IDNs. By means of the 16-bit alias IDNs, it is possible to parameterize the functionality accessible via EIDNs via a conventional communication interface which cannot handle 32bit EIDNs. 

P-0-2300 contains the list of those EIDNs for which 16-bit alias IDNs have been defined. The list is displayed in hexadecimal form and classified in as‐ cending order. For each entry there is a corresponding entry in P-0-2301 which indicates the associated 16-bit alias IDN.

## 4.15.385 P-0-2842, Force control deviation 

Allocation Contained in 21VRS: «MPB» «-» «-» «MPC» «-» Hardware -- -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: axis-specific Function The force control deviation indicates the current control quality of the control, thus the difference between P-0-0069 (Effective torque/force command val‐ ue) and P-0-2846.0.5 (Torque/force actual value filtered). 

Use 

With the help of this parameter you can control the regulation. That is, how precise is the control, or how fast is a disturbance compensated.

## 4.15.386 P-0-2843, Force controller output 

|Allocation|Contained in 21VRS:|«MPB»|«-»|«-»|«MPC»|«-»|
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
||Hardware|--|||||
||Funct. package(s):|SYX|||||
||Device parameter:|axis-specific|||||



Function 

Use 

The output of the force controller is the sum of the force controller compo‐ nents. Force control terms: P-term P-0-2846.0.1, I-term P-0-2846.0.2 and feedforward term P-0-2846.0.3. The output of the force controller can be in‐ verted via a bit in the force controller control word, parameter P-0-2840. 

The output of the force controller is used in the switching logic. There, differ‐ ent switching criteria are used to check whether the output of the position controller or the position controller is passed on to the distance adaptation.

## 4.15.387 P-0-2844, Force controller velocity feedforward 

Allocation Contained in 21VRS: «MPB» «-» «-» «MPC» «-» Hardware -- Funct. package(s): SYX Device parameter: axis-specific 

> Function It is possible to activate a velocity feedforward by describing the parameter with a constant or dynamically. 

> Use This functionality is used, for example, when an axis is moved but must not exceed a certain force limit value. The dynamic velocity connection relieves the I-term of the force controller and increases the control quality. If the veloc‐ ity feedforward is not active in this situation, the actual force value oscillates above the command value, since the I-term has to be reduced. If the function is active, the actual force value does not overshoot and the i-term only com‐ pensates for small differences.

## 4.15.396 P-0-2873.0.1, Valve standard velocity 

Allocation 

> Function The valve standard velocity is part of controller output adjustment. The travel velocity is specified at 100% valve opening. 

The controller generates velocity as output variable. In controller output ad‐ justment, this velocity is standardized via the valve standard velocity to the valve opening in %. 

In case of a standard valve velocity of 0, each controller control variable is standardized to a valve opening of 0%.

## 4.15.404 P-0-2873.0.9, Characteristic of flow 

> Function This parameter contains the list of input values for valve compensation. 

In most cases, an inflection is compensated this way to ensure linear behav‐ ior of the valve. The input value must contain the flow in percentage specified through the controller. The opening of the valve in percent is entered in the dedicated line at the output value. The length of input and output values must be identical and each line is a related value pair. Linear interpolation is ap‐ plied between the set values. 

Bosch Rexroth AG R911328651_Edition 15 

IndraDrive MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB Parameters 

889/1717 

Product-specific parameters 

Use 

If, for example, the valve has an inflection at 40% of the valve control variable and at 10% flow, then 10% has to be set for the flow as input value and 40% as output value. 

A setting of 0% and 100% is also recommended for interpolation between these points.

With this ramp, changes to the valve standard velocity are smoothed. In this respect, low values refer to a slow and high values to a quick change.

## 4.15.431 P-0-2945, Configuration of analog mode 

Allocation 

Contained in 20VRS: «MPB» «MPE» «MPM» «MPC» «-» Contained in 21VRS: «MPB» «-» «MPM» «MPC» «-» Hardware -- -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: axis-specific 

> Function On devices with analog master communication or deactivated Multi-Ethernet master communication, this parameter is used for configuring analog opera‐ tion. 

See also Functional Description "Analog interface" 

Structure 

The individual bits have the following significance: 

|Bit|Designation/function|Comment|
|---|---|---|
|0|Activation of controller enable<br>0:Edge-controlled signal<br>1:State-controlled signal||
|1|Automatic setting of controller enable in condition "Ab"<br>0:Not active<br>1:Active|"P-0-4028; bit<br>15" must not<br>be cyclically<br>configured.|
|2|Activation of controller enable by enable cable<br>0:Not active<br>1:Active|HydraulicDrive<br>only!<br>"P-0-4028; bit<br>15" must not<br>be cyclically<br>configured.|



Tab. 4-247: Relevant bits of P‑0‑2945 

## **WARNING** 

State-controlled controller enable! 

If analog operation is configured for "state-controlled controller enable", the drive automatically switches to drive control after a drive error was cleared, if the configured digital input or the enable cable is set. This can cause a move‐ ment of the axis! 

## **WARNING** 

## Automatic run-up 

If analog operation is configured for "automatic after run-up", the drive switches to closed-loop control immediately after running up. This can cause a movement of the axis! 

Use 

## Activation of controller enable (bit 0) 

For activating the controller enable, parameter "P-0-4028; bit 15" has to be configured for a digital input. 

Bosch Rexroth AG R911328651_Edition 15 

IndraDrive MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB Parameters 

899/1717 

Product-specific parameters 

- Edge-controlled: With a positive edge of the digital input the drive switches to closed-loop control. In the case of an error, the error has to be acknowledged first. Afterwards the drive can only be switched to closed-loop control operation with a new positive edge at the digital in‐ put. 

- State-controlled: State “1” at the digital input switches the drive to closed-loop control, as long as this is not prevented by any error. When an error is acknowledged, the drive automatically switches again to the closed-loop control mode as long as the digital input is still set. 

Automatic setting of controller enable (bit 1) 

After having run up to the state "Ab" the drive automatically switches to closed-loop control (AF). If an error occurs, the drive enable is reset. 

After command "C0500, Reset class 1 diagnostics" was executed for clearing any present error, the drive remains in state "Ab" and requires again an edge (e.g. switching from PM -> OM) to set the controller enable when bit 0 = 0 (edge-controlled) is set. With bit 0 = 1 (state-controlled), the drive activates the controller enable immediately after the error was cleared. 

Activation of controller enable by enable cable (bit 2) 

With HydraulicDrive it is possible to set the drive enable by means of a spe‐ cial hardware enable cable. 

With a positive edge of the enable cable, command "C0500, Reset class 1 diagnostics" is executed first and then the drive enable is activated. If an error occurs, the drive enable is reset. 

If, while drive enable is active, the enable cable is reset, the drive signals "F2025, Drive not ready for control".

## 4.16.37 P-0-3044, Motor torque at nominal current with reluctance, type plate 

Allocation 

Function 

|Contained in 18VRS:|«MPB»|«MPE»|«MPM»|«MPC»||
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|Contained in 20VRS:|«MPB»|«MPE»|«MPM»|«MPC»|«-»|
|Contained in 21VRS:|«MPB»|«-»|«MPM»|«MPC»|«-»|
|Hardware|--|||||
|Funct. package(s):|--|||||
|Device parameter:|axis-specific|||||



If the reluctance torque is used, the available motor torque is increased while the current remains the same. This requires an appropriate motor construc‐ tion. If reluctance is used at nominal current, parameter "P-0-3940" specifies the corresponding torque and/or force developed by the motor if the reluc‐ tance effect is utilized. The current to which the torque refers, is entered in parameter "S-0-0111, Motor current at standstill". 

The value of the torque must be higher than the torque calculated from the product of: 

P-0-0051, Torque/force constant * S-0-0111, Motor current at standstill

Parameter "P-0-3052" is used to display the thermal operating data of the motor stored in the encoder data memory. 

The parameter is read-only and cannot be changed by the cus‐ tomer. 

This parameter is only available for Rexroth motors with QEM encoder data memory version 4 (MSK) and 7 (MS2N). It displays the thermal operating da‐ ta of the motor stored in the encoder. Refer to "Structure". 

The thermal operating data are determined by the controller at 2-ms intervals (P-0-2052) and stored hourly to the active, non-volatile parameter memory. However, "P-0-3052" is only updated after the control voltage supply has been switched on by storing the value of "P-0-2052" to"P-0-3052" if necessa‐ ry. 

- To ensure that the current operating data of the motor that is stored in the controller can be filed to the encoder data memory in servicing cases, the control voltage has to be switched on again before the motor is replaced. 

- The above-mentioned Rexroth motors do not allow resetting the thermal operating data!

Function

|Device parameter:|axis-specific|||||



This parameter defines the temperature difference by which the motor shut‐ down temperature is reduced by the temperature model depending on the current speed. The data are specified according to the currently set tempera‐ ture scaling based on 1000 revolutions per minute. 

Example: For scaling in degrees Celsius, a value of 3.0 in this parameter de‐ fines that the motor shutdown temperature is to be reduced by 3.0 °C at a speed of 1000 rpm. 

Speed-dependent motor shutdown temperature reduction is initialized de‐ pending on the mounting situation from the respective list element in parame‐ ter "P-0-3060.0.5". The mounting position is defined in "P-0-3060.0.4". 

For Bosch Rexroth motors, the parameters required for initializa‐ tion of "P-0-3060.0.3" are read from the encoder memory. For third-party motors, "P-0-3060.0.3" can be configured directly.

> Function Performing the machine acceptance test in the "error reaction" testing point requires to check the drive reaction to safety technology errors occurring. Specifically for this purpose, this parameter features the option of generating F3 and/or F7 errors. 

Bit 0 and bit 1 are evaluated every time the parameter "P-0-3211" is written. If a bit has been set, the error belonging to the bit is generated once per write request.

|Device parameter:|axis-specific|||||



> Function The parameter defines the percentage evaluation factor for calculating the velocity limit value of the positioning operation modes when using Safe Mo‐ tion. 

The velocity limit value is derived from the product of "P-0-3238, SMO: active velocity threshold "and "P-0-3218, SMO: Scaling fac‐ tor for velocity limit value". The limit value is usually reduced by "P-0-3255, SMO: Velocity threshold safe standstill" compared with the active velocity threshold. 

See also "P-0-3219, SMO: Configuration of support functions"

> Function The scaling type of the position data determines the format and the relation in which the position data are exchanged between the drive and the control or user interface. The values of the position data parameters (e.g. P-0-3257, SMO: Position feedback value) are displayed by the drive with the set scal‐ ing. The scaling setting is usually defined by the control. 

Any change in the parameter setting has an effect on the scaling of the safety technology. Such a change therefore has an effect on the display and processing of velocity, position or acceleration data in the safety technology. 

It is advisable to parameterize the parameter in the same way as "S-0-0076" of the standard firmware.

## 4.17.40 P-0-3230.0.1, SMO: Password 

Allocation 

> Function Parameter "P-0-3230.0.1" can be used to activate the safety technology. The password serves to disable and enable write access to all relevant safety technology parameters. 

> Structure Password inputs. ● At least 3 characters and no more than 10 characters long 

● permissible characters are "A - Z", "a - z" and numerals "0 - 9" If the safety technology password is not as specified, the password entered is discarded. 

The initial password "INDRASAVE" and parameter "P-0-3235.0.1, SMO: Active axis identifier" are not accepted as safety technology password. 

Safety technology passwords are handled with the assistance of dialog boxes in the "IndraWorks Ds/D/MLD" commissioning soft‐ ware.

> Function This parameter controls axis identification. Via bits 0 and 1, identification is activated. The axis reacts with an optical signal. In this state, identification can be confirmed by starting "P-0-3235.0.3, C8500 SMO: Command Apply identification data". When executing command C8500, the identification data is with the bit in "P-0-3235.0.4" set to "1" is applied. After successful com‐ mand execution, the bits are reset to "0".

> Function Bipolar tolerance range for safe homing. The tolerance range is applied for different independent monitoring functions: 

During command C4000: 

- The plausibility of the position at which the SMO reference signal is rec‐ ognized is validated with "P-0-3253.0.3 SMO: Reference position" +/this tolerance range. 

- It is checked that the distance between the SMO reference signal and the reference switch of the standard firmware is at least as high as this tolerance range multiplied by a factor of 2. 

After the safe reference is established: 

- For monitoring of the SMO reference signal for "stuck at high": Outside of the SMO reference position (P-0-3253.0.3) +/- this tolerance range, the SMO reference signal has to be on low level. 

At cyclic checking of the safe reference: 

- On triggering the reference event, the SMO position feedback value has to be in the range of "P-0-3253.0.3, SMO: Reference position" +/- this tolerance range.

If "Cyclic check of safe reference" is configured (P-0-3253.0.1) and the SMO reference signal (P-0-3253.0.0) is not recognized within the admissible posi‐ tion range (P-0-3253.0.3 ± P-0-3253.0.4) within this time interval, "Safe refer‐ ence of the SMO encoder" is lost (P-0-3256). In addition, error message F3166 is generated. 

The check is only performed if the velocity feedback value is below the veloc‐ ity threshold (P-0-3253.0.5) (same criteria for clear recognition at C4000). 

The time interval is restarted if the SMO reference signal is detected in the allowed range or if the error F3166 is cleared.

## 4.17.106 P-0-3263.0.8, SMO: SMD-E jerk 

Allocation 

Function 

Contained in 20VRS: «MPB» «-» «MPM» «MPC» «-» Contained in 21VRS: «MPB» «-» «MPM» «MPC» «-» Hardware S3, S4, S5, SB, SD -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: axis-specific 

The parameter defines the maximum allowed jerk that is taken into account in the velocity envelope curve for the monitoring of the drive-controlled error re‐ action, with velocity command value reset with ramp and filter, after F3 and F7 errors. 

With the value 0, the jerk is not taken into account. 

The parameter is used in the safety functions "Safely-limited end position (SLE)" and "Safely-limited position (SLP)" to calculate the maximum allowed approach velocity to the parameterized position limits. 

When using the jerk (P-0-3263.0.8 > 0), the value in "P-0-3263.0.8" should be set to the jerk limit value of the standard firmware in the parameter "S-0-0349, Jerk limit bipolar" and the value in "P-0-3263.0.3, SMO: Delay SMD-E" can be parameter‐ ized to the delay ramp of the standard firmware in "S-0-0429, Emergency stop delay".

Bit 2 and 3 are updated in the SI operating state with active "Safely-limited position n (SLP)" or "Safely-monitored position n (SMP)" safety function and in error state after occurrence of error F7011/F7012 as long as the error-causing SI operating state is selected.

## **WARNING** 

Lethal injury and/or property damage caused by unintended axis motion! 

⇒ If the brake is manually controlled via the "release holding brake" control signal, the drive is no longer able to counteract external force influences. In this state, the safety technology does not carry out any monitoring function! 

If external force influences are to be expected, e.g. in the case of a vertical axis, this motion has to be safely prevented by additional measures, e.g. a counterweight.

R911328651_Edition 15 Bosch Rexroth AG 

IndraDrive MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB Parameters 

994/1717 

Product-specific parameters 

> Function The parameter provides binary control signals for online control of the safe brake via digital hardware inputs (local safe inputs). 

Structure 

|Bit|Designation/function|Comment|
|---|---|---|
|0|Release holding system<br>0:Not active (default)<br>1:Active||
|1|Enabling signal special mode without valid brake status<br>0:Not active (default)<br>1:Active|MPx-21V04<br>and above|
|2|Signal for temporarily deactivating load torque monitoring<br>0:Not active (default)<br>1:Active|MPx-21V06<br>and above|



Tab. 4-289: SMO: Control word of safe braking and holding function 

> Use Bit 0: The holding system can be controlled via the signal "Release holding system" if the SBC function is active, if "P-0-3265.0.1; bit 1 = 1" and if the safety technology operating status of special mode "Safe standstill" with STO is active. 

Bit 1: Via the "Enabling signal special mode without valid brake status" switching to special mode is possible without error message F3123 if the sta‐ tus "monitoring holding system = not OK" reports (P-0-3265.0.0, bit 10). Enable: limited to 15 minutes from the first 0-1 edge. Once the enable dura‐ tion is terminated, a safe brake test has to be executed successfully (com‐ mand C21) before a new use. The signal must not be set during the safe brake test (command C21). Otherwise, the command is canceled with an error message. Prerequisite: Functionality is enabled/intended use is config‐ ured (P-0-3292.0.1, bit 11). 

Bit 2: Load torque monitoring can temporarily be disabled via bit 2. 

It has to be ensured that the axis comes to standstill once per brake test interval outside areas in which load torque monitoring is disabled. 

The signal must not be set during the safe brake test (command C21). Other‐ wise, the command is canceled with an error message. During deactivation, the determination of the load torque continues, so that the value in the "P-0-3294, SMO: Load torque/force actual value" is still available for diagnos‐ tic purposes. Prerequisite: Functionality is enabled/intended use is configured (P-0-3292.0.1, bit 14). 

Permanently switching off the load torque monitoring results in the diagnostic coverage dropping to 60 % for the monitored brakes. Sporadically, "SIL3" or "PL e" cannot be achieved any‐ more.

## 4.17.115 P-0-3266, SMO: Status word safety zone 

Allocation Contained in 18VRS: «MPB» «-» «MPM» «MPC» Contained in 20VRS: «MPB» «-» «MPM» «MPC» «-» Contained in 21VRS: «MPB» «-» «MPM» «MPC» «-» Hardware S4, S5 -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: axis-specific 

Function 

This parameter displays the information which the zone node delivers to the zone bus (bits 0 and 1) for diagnostic purposes. This information is formed from the status of the preceding zone nodes (bits 4 and 5) and the status of the zone node itself (bits 8 and 9). 

In addition, it displays enabling of normal operation (bit 2) which is only es‐ tablished by the zone master. The states shown here do not lead to an axis reaction of the zone node. tThese are shown in "P-0-3266.0.1, SMO: Safety zone control word". 

Structure 

|Bit|Designation/function|Comment|
|---|---|---|
|0|Safety on following zone nodes(out, X43)<br>0:Zone is not safe<br>1:Zone is safe||
|1|Error on following zone nodes(out, X43)<br>0:Zone error present<br>1:Zone error not present||
|2|Enabling of normal operation (only zone master)(out,<br>X43)<br>0:Normal operation disabled<br>1:Normal operation enabled||

## 4.17.119 P-0-3266.0.4, SMO: Tolerance time for Safe door locking 

> Function The maximum tolerated delay between the control of the door locking device and the door locking feedback (P-0-3266.0.3) in the case of state changes is set using "P-0-3266.0.4, SMO: Tolerance time for Safe door locking". 

The parameter has to be set in such a way that both the delays in the case of door locking state changes and any contact bouncing of the feedback signals are taken into account.

## 4.17.122 P-0-3270.0.3, SMO: Standstill window for Safe direction 

Allocation Contained in 18VRS: «MPB» «-» «MPM» «MPC» Contained in 20VRS: «MPB» «-» «MPM» «MPC» «-» Contained in 21VRS: «MPB» «-» «MPM» «MPC» «-» Hardware S3, S4, S5, SB, SD -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: axis-specific 

> Function The parameter (consideration of encoder noise) is used as position monitor‐ ing window for direction monitoring in various safety functions. 

- In the safety function "Safe direction (SDI)", the value defines the maxi‐ mum allowed travel distance in the non-enabled direction, in relation to the actual position taken at the time of activation of the safety function. If the "standstill window for safe direction" is left in the non-enabled di‐ rection, the error F7031 is generated. 

- ● In the safety function "Safe CAM (SCA)", the parameter is used as a switching hysteresis to prevent the cam status display at the cam limit from flickering (due to encoder noise). Entering a cam range or exiting it occurs after the parameterized switching hysteresis was passed. The switching hysteresis that has been set takes effect on all cams. 

- ● In the following safety functions, the parameter is applied as a monitor‐ ing window for the return to the allowed position range. 

   - Safely-limited end position (SLE) 

   - – Safely-limited position (SLP) 

   - – Safely-monitored position (SMP) The value defines the maximum allowed travel distance in the nonenabled direction in relation to the previous actual position (tracked threshold). 

If the monitoring window is left in the non-enabled direction, the safety function-specific position limit value error is generated again:

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|||–|F7012 SMP, SLP: Safe position limit value, negative exceeded||||

## 4.17.123 P-0-3270.0.4, SMO: Safe end position limit value, positive 

Allocation 

Contained in 20VRS: «MPB» «-» «MPM» «MPC» «-» Contained in 21VRS: «MPB» «-» «MPM» «MPC» «-» Hardware S3, S4, S5, SB, SD -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: axis-specific 

> Function The allowed travel range of an axis can be defined by position limit values. The "safe end position limit value, where positive" defines the maximum ad‐ missible position feedback value in positive direction. 

Bosch Rexroth AG R911328651_Edition 15 

IndraDrive MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB Parameters 

1001/1717 

Product-specific parameters 

The parameterized position limits (P-0-3270.0.4 and P-0-3270.0.5) are sub‐ ject to dual-channel monitored with the "Safely-limited end position (SLE)" function if it has been configured in "P-0-3270.0.1" or "P-0-3277.0.1". 

The following aspects have to be observed for use: 

- Monitoring of the "Safely-limited end position (SLE)" will not become ef‐ fective before the drive has been safely homed (P-0-3256; bit 0). 

- If the safety function recognizes faulty behavior during "Safely-limited end position" monitoring, error message F7023 or F7024 are returned. The drive is shut down with the configured F7 error reaction (torque dis‐ able is not admissible as F7 error reaction).

> Function The "Safe CAM 1" can be parameterized in this list parameter. 

The status of the multiple cams 1 to 8 and of the single cams 1 to 16 is displayed in "P-0-3273.0.1, SMO: Status word, bit-coded SCA". 

The status of the single cams 1 to 31 is displayed in "P-0-3273.0.0, SMO: Status word, binary-coded SCA".

- 1: Cam evaluation in positive direction 

- 2: Cam evaluation in negative direction 

- 3: Cam evaluation in both directions 

The switch-on threshold of cam 1 is parameterized in the list element 1.

> Function This parameter serves to configure the "safety-monitored deceleration (SMD)" safety function based on the actual velocity. 

The "SMD-E reaction time" is the reaction time for the system (control and drive) in order that the command value input can be adjusted for the transfer to the selected special mode. After this time has elapsed, the parameterized deceleration ramp is monitored. 

See also: Safely-Monitored Deceleration (SMD)

Allocation 

Function at "Safe operating stFuncti **o** pn With the "Safe operating stop (SOS)" safety function, this parameter is ap‐ SOS" plied to define the maximum admissible travel distance in positive or negative direction (monitoring window). The monitoring window refers to the actual po‐ sition of the drive on activation of "Safe operating stop (SOS)". 

If the parameterized monitoring window is left, error "F7030 Position window for safe operating stop exceeded" is generated.

## 4.17.182 P-0-3290.x.3, SMO: Safely-limited increment 

> Function This parameter defines a relative position window for the "Special mode "Safe Motion" n" (n = 1-16). This window is spread on start of the "Special mode "Safe Motion" n" (n = 1-16) . For duration of the "Special mode "Safe Motion" n" (n = 1-16), the drive can be freely moved within this position win‐ dow. If the function "Safely-limited increment" is activated in "Special mode "Safe Motion" n" (n = 1-16), the error message F7010 Safely-limited incre‐ ment exceeded is emitted if this position window is exceeded.

## 4.17.183 P-0-3290.x.4, SMO: Safe position limit value, positive 

Allocation 

Function 

|Contained in 20VRS:|«MPB»|«-»|«MPM»|«MPC»|«-»|
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|Contained in 21VRS:|«MPB»|«-»|«MPM»|«MPC»|«-»|
|Hardware|S3, S4, S5, SB, SD|||||
|Funct. package(s):|--|||||
|Device parameter:|axis-specific|||||



The allowed travel range of an axis can be defined by position limit values. The "safe position limit value, positive" defines the maximum admissible posi‐ tion feedback value for "special operation safe motion n" (n = 1-16) in positive direction. 

Depending on the configuration in P-0-3290.x.1, the parameterized position limits (P-0-3290.x.4 and P-0-3290.x.5) are subject to dual-channel monitoring using the functions "Safely-monitored position (SMP)" (P-0-3290.x.1; bit 5 = 1) or "Safely-limited position (SLP)" (P-0-3290.x.1; bit 7 = 1 ). 

The following aspects have to be observed for use: 

- Monitoring of the "Safely-monitored position (SLP)" and "Safely-limited position (SLP)" will not become effective before the drive has been safe‐ ly homed (P-0-3256; bit 0). 

- If the safety function recognizes faulty behavior during "Safely-moni‐ tored position (SMP)" or "Safely-limited position (SLP)" monitoring, error message F7011 or F7012 are returned. The drive is shut down with the configured F7 error reaction (torque disable is not admissible as F7 error reaction for safety function "Safely-limited position (SLP)").

> Function This parameter defines a velocity threshold (bipolar) for "Safely-monitored transient oscillation" in "Special mode safe motion n" (n = 1-16). ## 4.17.196 P-0-3293.x.0, SMO: SBT_stat, brake position window 

Allocation 

Contained in 21VRS: «MPB» «-» «MPM» «MPC» «-» Hardware S4, S5, SB, SD -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: axis-specific 

> Function In this parameter, the admissible position window / travel range can be en‐ tered for testing of the holding capacity for brake 1 / brake 2. 

An admissible position window is required to take into account the torsion and play in the system. Particularly brakes installed on the load side can have a considerable deflection during the brake test. 

When checking for unrestricted movement, the axis has to be moved by the position window at least to pass the test. 

> Use The structure index (SI) is applied to determine the brake: 

● SI="1": Brake 1 

- SI="2": Brake 2

## 4.17.206 P-0-3297.x.0, SMO: SBT_stat, test load factor for wear test 

Allocation 

Contained in 21VRS: «MPB» «-» «MPM» «MPC» «-» Hardware S4, S5, SB, SD -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: axis-specific 

> Function After checking the holding capacity of brake 1 / brake 2, an integrated wear test can be carried out with a test load factor exceeding the safety factor. 

In P-0-3297.x.0, a test load factor for wear test can be preset. 

P-0-3297.x.0 is not a secure parameter! 

For this wear test, command C2100 has to be started with P-0-0538, bit 6="1". 

The test load for the wear test is calculated as follows:

Product-specific parameters 

Test load for wear test = 

Nominal load x Safety factor x Test load factor for wear test P-0-3292.0.3 × P-0-3292.0.4 × P-0-3297.x.0

## 4.17.216 P-0-3322.0.3, SMO: Periodic time of local input X(1)41 

Allocation 

Contained in 21VRS: «MPB» «-» «MPM» «MPC» «-» Hardware S3, S4, S5, SD -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: axis-specific Alias: P-0-3841 

> Function If one or both local inputs of the optional safety technology module are con‐ figured as safe inputs [X41 (X41.1 and X41.2 for double-axis devices), X141 for IndraDrive Mi], the signals (with signal level = "1") must be provided with regular test pulses. 

In this parameter, the maximum periodic time of the test pulses can be con‐ figured for both local inputs. 

● At least one test pulse must occur per periodic time. 

● There is only one maximum periodic time for both inputs.

## 4.17.228 P-0-3332.0.3, SMO: Functional inputs, test pulse width 

Allocation 

> Function The functional inputs 13... 16 (P-0-3329, Bit 12… 15) are accepted as dyna‐ mized functional signals. 

With activated dynamization (P-0-3332.0.4 > "0"), the signals (signal level = "1") must be provided with regular test pulses. 

In "P-0-3332.0.3", the maximum length (in ms) of the occurring test pulses can be set. The maximum test pulse length sets the reaction time for recogni‐ tion of deactivation of dynamization monitoring.

## 4.17.229 P-0-3332.0.4, SMO: Functional inputs, periodic time of test pulses 

Allocation Contained in 20VRS: «MPB» «-» «MPM» «MPC» «-» Contained in 21VRS: «MPB» «-» «MPM» «MPC» «-» Hardware S3, S4, S5, SB, SD -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: axis-specific Alias: P-0-3747 Function The functional inputs 13... 16 (P-0-3329; bit 12… 15) are accepted as dyna‐ mized functional signals.

## 4.17.239 P-0-3336.0.5, SMO: Signal control status safety bus, SMMx coding 

Allocation Contained in 18VRS: «MPB» «-» «MPM» «MPC» Contained in 20VRS: «MPB» «-» «MPM» «MPC» «-» Contained in 21VRS: «MPB» «-» «MPM» «MPC» «-» Hardware S3, S4, S5, SB, SD -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: axis-specific Alias: P-0-2529 

> Function The "Special mode safe motion x (SMM x)" source signals from "P-0-3231, SMO: Operating status" are bit-encoded. Depending on the type of preferen‐ tial configuration of the status word Safety bus, the status for special mode safe motion is contained there either with bit or binary coding. 

The coding function is parameterized in this parameter. If a value unequal to 0 is entered here, the coding in the "signal control for status word Safety bus" function is bit-to-binary. The number of source signals is then parameterized in this parameter.

||8 - 5|Binary coding active SMM1 / 8-5 to 3 bit<br>outputs|3-bit-coded inP-0-3341, 2<br>following bits assigned|

## 4.17.240 P-0-3340, SMO: Safety bus control word 

|Allocation|Contained in 18VRS:|«MPB»|«-»|«MPM»|«MPC»||

||Hardware|S3, S4, S5, SB, SD|||||
||Funct. package(s):|--|||||
||Device parameter:|axis-specific|||||



> Function This parameter is used to transmit control information of a safety control via safe bus communication as a part of the consumer connection. The evalua‐ tion of the individual bits of the "control word Safety bus" depends on the con‐ figuration of the IO mapper inputs (P-0-3330.x.y). 

Only preferential configurations are supported at present; there‐ fore the "IO mapper inputs" are configured automatically. 

If "P-0-3340.0.1, SMO: Mask of Control word Safety-Bus" is used to mask bits, the respective bit of the control word is not imple‐ mented to the target parameter 1:1. A user-side setting for evalu‐ ation of the bit can be configured in the IO mapper.

The parameter displays the active PROFIsafe F-Device address. For safe ad‐ dress assignment (P-0-3235.0.3), the value of the parameter is applied from the parameter "P-0-3360.0.2", that was input before, and saved in the identifi‐ cation data image on the programming module.

## 4.18.3 P-0-3602.0.1, CiA301: COB-ID SYNC message 

Allocation Contained in 20VRS: «MPB» «-» «-» «MPC» «PSB» Contained in 21VRS: «MPB» «-» «-» «MPC» «PSB» Hardware CoC -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: axis-specific 

> Function This parameters implements the object 1005h "COB ID SYNC message" for the profile "CiA301". 

The object defines the COB ID of the synchronization object (SYNC). It also defines whether the device generates the Sync telegram. 

Structure 

Index 1005h, subindex 0 for "COB ID SYNC message" 

|Bit|Name/function|Comment|
|---|---|---|
|28…0|CAN ID<br>80h|Die CAN ID of the Sync telegram is 80h<br>by default.|
|29|Frame<br>0b: 11-bit CAN ID||
|30|CANopen device generates the<br>Sync telegram<br>0b: CANopen device does not<br>generate the Sync telegram<br>1b: CANopen device generates<br>the Sync telegram|Generally, the CANopen master sends<br>the Sync telegram. In this case, the<br>CANopen device is the receiver of the<br>Sync telegram ("Sync Consumer"and is<br>then synchronized as slave via the Sync<br>telegram by the master).<br>In special cases, the CANopen device<br>can sent the Sync telegram and allows<br>other CANopen devices to synchronize<br>with it ("Sync Producer").|
|31|Not relevant||



Example: 

As "Sync consumer" , the object value is 00000080h by default. 

As "Sync producer" , the object value is 40000080h by default.

## 4.18.8 P-0-3605.0.1, CiA301: Guard time 

Allocation 

Contained in 20VRS: «MPB» «-» «-» «MPC» «PSB» Contained in 21VRS: «MPB» «-» «-» «MPC» «PSB» Hardware CoC -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: axis-specific 

> Function This parameters implements the object 100Ch "Guard time" for the profile "CiA301". 

The object contains the "Guard time" in milliseconds. 

Use the "Guard time" and the "Life time factor" to calculate the "life time" for the node guarding protocol to monitor the node as follows: 

Life time [ms] = Guard time [ms] × Life time factor 

Guard time: 100Ch (P-0-3605.0.1) 

Life time factor: 100Dh (P-0-3605.0.2) 

If the device is not queried by the master using the guarding telegram within the "life time", a monitoring error is generated. 

If the "life time" is "0", "node guarding" is disabled.

Bosch Rexroth AG R911328651_Edition 15 

IndraDrive MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB Parameters

As "heartbeat consumer", the slave monitors the "heartbeat" of the master. The object indexes the maximum cycle time expected by the "master heart‐ beat" in milliseconds. If the slave did not receive any "heartbeat" from the master within this period, a monitoring error is generated.

## 4.18.24 P-0-3608.x.3, CiA301: Transmission type RPDO 

Allocation Contained in 20VRS: «MPB» «-» «-» «MPC» «PSB» Contained in 21VRS: «MPB» «-» «-» «MPC» «PSB» Hardware CoC -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: axis-specific Function The parameters implement the objects from 1400h to 1403h "RPDO communication parameter", subindex 2 "Transmission type RPDO" for the profile "CiA301". 

Allocation 

The transmission method of the respective RPDO can be set via the parame‐ ter. 

|P-0-3608.0.3|Index 1400h, subindex 2 for RPDO1|
|---|---|
|P-0-3608.1.3|Index 1401h, subindex 2 for RPDO2|
|P-0-3608.2.3|Index 1402h, subindex 2 for RPDO3|
|P-0-3608.3.3|Index 1403h, subindex 2 for RPDO4|



## Supported transmission methods 

Type 0 synchronous, acyclic 

The RPDO is sent by the master if required ("event-driven"). Data received in the slave is processed after the next Sync telegram. 

Type 1 synchronous, cyclic 

The RPDO is sent in each Sync cycle by the master. Data received in the slave is processed after the next Sync telegram. 

Type 254 Synchronous, acyclic 

The RPDO is sent by the master if required ("event-driven"). Data received in the slave is processed as soon as possible.

|P-0-3614.3.3|Index 1803h, subindex 2 for TPDO4|



## Supported transmission methods 

Type 0 synchronous, acyclic The TPDO is sent by the slave if required ("event-driven") after the next Sync point. Type 1 synchronous, cyclic The TPDO is cyclically sent by the slave after each Sync point. Type 252 synchronous, RTR-only Data of the TDPO is refreshed in each Sync cycle. The TPDO is not actively send, only upon an RTR request. Type 254 Synchronous, acyclic The TPDO is sent by the slave only if required ("event-driven"). 

"Event-driven" : An event is available if data changed in the PDO. If data changes continuously, the "inhibit time" (subindex 3) (P-0-3614.x.4) applies to ensure that the PDO is not sent more of‐ ten than this inhibit time. If data changes rarely or not at all, the PDO is still sent after the time "event timer" (subindex 5) (P-0-3614.x.5) elapses.

## 4.18.37 P-0-3614.x.4, CiA301: Inhibit time TPDO 

Allocation 

Contained in 20VRS: «MPB» «-» «-» «MPC» «PSB» Contained in 21VRS: «MPB» «-» «-» «MPC» «PSB» Hardware CoC -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: axis-specific 

> Function The parameters implement the objects from 1800h to 1803h "TPDO communication parameter", subindex 3 "Inhibit time TPDO" for the profile "CiA301". 

Via the parameter, a minimum time span in microseconds [µs] can be defined for the "event-driven" TPDO. Even if the event occurs more often, the TPDO is not sent more often than this time span in order not to overload the field bus. 

"Inhibit time TPDO" should be a multiple of 100 µs and lower than "event timer TPDO" (P-0-3614.x.6).

## 4.18.39 P-0-3614.x.200, TPDO on-event bit mask 

Allocation 

Function 

Contained in 21VRS: «MPB» «-» «-» «MPC» «PSB» Hardware CoC -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: axis-specific Alias: P-0-3894, P-0-3895, P-0-3896, P-0-3897 

The parameter allows for an additional configuration for "event-driven" TPDOs for the "CiA301" profile for the objects 1800h to 1803h "TPDO communication parameter". 

The P-0-3614.x.200 provides a bit mask to define which bits of the TPDO are considered for generating an event for sending. By default all bits of the mask are set and all bits of the TPDO are considered for the generation of events. If a bit of the mask is set to 0 , a change of the bit at the same position in the TPDO does not generate an event anymore. 

"Event-driven”: An event is present when the data in the PDO has changed. This parameter allows to limit the generation of events to the change of certain data in the PDO. This can be used, for example, if only the change of a certain process date is relevant for the application.

Product-specific parameters 

Use 

|P-0-3615.0.1|Index 1A00h, subindex 0 for TPDO1|
|---|---|

|Example:||



Number 0: Mapping disabled. The PDO is thus disabled. Number 1: Object of the subindex 1 is valid. 

Number 2: Objects of the subindices 1 to 2 are valid. Number 3: Objects of the subindices 1 to 3 are valid. Number 4: Objects of the subindices 1 to 4 are valid. 

Subindex 1 up to subindex 4 are the valid maximum. 

Proceed as follows for the PDO mapping: 

1. Set subindex 0 to "0" to delete all existing mapping objects in this PDO. 

2. Write from subindex 1 up to subindex N (N ≤ 4) with mapping objects. 

3. Set the subindex 0 to the number N.

## 4.18.51 P-0-3618.0.1, ECAT: Receive PDO Mapping 

Allocation 

Function 

Contained in 20VRS: «MPB» «MPE» «-» «MPC» «PSB» Contained in 21VRS: «MPB» «-» «-» «MPC» «PSB» Hardware CoE -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: axis-specific 

CAN over EtherCAT (CoE) object according to /CiA301/ 

Index 1600h "Receive PDO Mapping Parameter" 

Subindex 0 - "number of mapped application objects in PDO" 

While reading, the number of valid entries of the application objects is re‐ turned to the subindex. When a certain value is written N (0 ≤ N ≤ 16) the entries of the application objects, which are available in subindices 1 to N, are mapped in the PDO channel. Subindices N+1 through 16 become invalid. See also parameter description "P-0-3619.0.1" 

|Value|Description|
|---|---|
|0|Mapping deactivated|
|1|Subindex 1 valid|
|2|Subindices 1 to 2 valid|
|3|Subindices 1 to 3 valid|
|......|......|
|16|Subindices 1 to 16 valid|

Allocation 

Function 

The Boolean flag signals whether or not the node ID of the Ethernet POWER‐ LINK drive can be set exclusively by means of hardware (HW) or software (SW). 

0 (FALSE) for drives, the node ID of which can be set exclusively by means of SW. 

1 (TRUE) for drives, the node ID of which can be set exclusively by means of HW.

## 4.18.131 P-0-3647.0.7, ECAT: Calc and Copy Time (Outputs) 

Allocation 

Function 

|Contained in 20VRS:|«MPB»|«MPE»|«-»|«MPC»|«PSB»|
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|Contained in 21VRS:|«MPB»|«-»|«-»|«MPC»|«PSB»|
|Hardware|CoE|||||
|Funct. package(s):|--|||||
|Device parameter:|axis-specific|||||



The command value (process data master → slave) is cyclically received by the slave from the EtherCAT FPGA and processed. This takes place one po‐ sition controller cycle before the Sync1 event. For this reason, the EtherCAT telegram with the command value is to be received one position controller cy‐ cle before the Sync1 event. The time of a position controller cycle varies de‐ pending on the device derivative and performance. This is designated "Calc and copy time (outputs)". 

CAN over EtherCAT (CoE) object 

Index 1C32h - "Output Sync manager parameter" 

Subindex 6 - "Calc and copy time (outputs)" 

The "Calc and copy time (outputs)" - object 1C32h subindex 6 - before the Sync1 event and the "Calc and copy time (inputs)" - object 1C33h subindex 6 - after the Sync1 event together form a protection time. During this protection time, the master must not send the EtherCAT telegram. 

See also parameter description "P-0-3648.0.7"

## 4.18.136 P-0-3648.0.7, ECAT: Calc and Copy Time (Inputs) 

CAN over EtherCAT (CoE) object 

Index 1C33h - "Input Sync manager parameter" 

Subindex 6 - "Calc and copy time (inputs)" 

The "Calc and copy time (outputs)" - object 1C32h subindex 6 - before the Sync1 event and the "Calc and copy time (inputs)" - object 1C33h subindex 6 - after the Sync1 event together form a protection time. During this protection time, the master must not send the EtherCAT telegram. 

See also parameter description "P-0-3647.0.7"

> Function This parameter contains the characteristic for temperature measurement of the power output stage, if this characteristic deviates from a nominal charac‐ teristic. The data are written during assembly and cannot be changed by the user. 

Structure 

The values must be strictly and monotonously ascending or descending, i.e. in the table the values assigned to an increasing temperature must either be always higher than all preceding values or always lower than all preceding values. In the table, the values must not descend and ascend in different sec‐ tions of the table!

## 4.18.243 P-0-3930, C7600 Command Create parameter image 

|Allocation|Contained in 17VRS:|«-»|«-»|«-»|«MPC»||
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
||Contained in 18VRS:|«MPB»|«MPE»|«MPM»|«MPC»||

||Hardware|--|||||
||Funct. package(s):|--|||||
||Device parameter:|device-specific|||||



> Function Parameter "P-0-3930" can be used to generate an image of the current drive parameter values in a file on the external memory card (SnapShot). The name of this file is always "SnapShot.par". The file is stored to the "Temp" folder of the memory card. 

This parameter image can comprise the data of a single axis (single backup) or the data of all axes connected in the CCD group (complete backup). The content of the parameter image can be created based on the parameter list "S-0-0017" or "S-0-0192". Image generation is configured in parameter "P-0-3931". 

The following information is saved from all ident numbers listed in the selec‐ ted reference parameter: 

- Ident number 

- Unit 

- Attribute 

- Operating data 

The backup file is stored in "sercos ASCII" format, i.e., it can be opened and evaluated in "IndraWorks". Execution of the command can be aborted by de‐ leting the command. If execution of the command is aborted, the associated backup file is deleted. The command "Create parameter image" is only avail‐ able for drive derivatives with a file system on the SD card.

Parameter "P-0-3933" contains the character string of the service password. 

After "Load basic parameter", the password: "serviceWeb" is active. The service password is used by the drive's ServiceTools (IMST, IDST). 

It can be set to prevent unauthorized persons from logging in as "service" user and gaining access to all service dialogs. 

A service password is set by writing the parameter "P-0-3933" via the com‐ missioning software "IndraWorks Ds". This is also where the encryption of the password takes place. This is checked during access to the IDST.

> Function If the reluctance torque is used, the available motor torque is increased while the current remains the same. This requires an appropriate motor construc‐ tion. The current to which the torque refers is specified in parameter "S-0-0111, Motor current at standstill". 

The torque value must be higher than the torque resulting from the product of:

|Funct. package(s):|--|||||

> Function Along with parameter "P-0-4003, Charact. of quadrature-axis inductance of motor, currents", this parameter describes the characteristic curve of the quadrature-axis inductance of the motor (Lq) in relation to the torque-generat‐ ing current (lq). 

If required (e.g. saturation phenomena), it is thereby possible to achieve a reduction of the effective current controller gain for higher currents. 

> Structure "P-0-4002" is designed as a list whose list elements each form value pairs with those of "P-0-4003"; these value pairs define the characteristic curve.

## Fig. 4-84: Significance and Function of P-0-4002 and P-0-4003 

The values in parameter "P-0-4002" are factors which refer to parameter "P-0-4017, Quadrature-axis inductance of motor". The inductance values Lq of the characteristic are resulting by multiplication with this value. 

## Use 

The parameter always has to contain 4 list elements. The values of these ele‐ ments have to be monotonously descending. 

The parameter is exclusively used when the "synchronous motor with reluctance torque" or "adjustment of current controller to sat‐ uration of quadrature-axis inductance of motor" bit is set in pa‐ rameter "P-0-4014, Type of construction of motor". 

Writing the correct value to this parameter: 

- By loading the motor parameters with commissioning soft‐ ware "IndraWorks Ds/D/MLD" in case of MBS high-speed motors by Bosch Rexroth. 

- By loading the value from the encoder data memory when the control voltage of the drive is switched on in case of MSK motors. 

- In case of all other Rexroth motors, use of the parameter is prevented by a setting of parameter "P-0-4014" that is auto‐ matically made in the firmware or by the commissioning soft‐ ware "IndraWorks Ds/D/MLD". 

- In case of other motors, manual input according to manufac‐ turer's specification.

> Function Along with parameter "P-0-4002, Charact. of quadrature-axis induct. of mo‐ tor, inductances", this parameter describes the characteristic curve of the quadrature-axis inductance of the motor Lq in relation to the torque-generat‐ ing current lq. 

If required (e.g. saturation phenomena), it is thereby possible to achieve a reduction of the effective current controller gain for higher currents. 

Structure 

P-0-4002 is designed as a list whose list elements each form value pairs with those of "P-0-4003"; these value pairs define the characteristic curve.

## 4.18.267 P-0-4010, Load inertia 

|Allocation|Contained in 16VRS:|«MPB»|«MPE»|«MPM»|||
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
||Contained in 17VRS:|«MPB»|«MPE»|«MPM»|«MPC»||
||Contained in 18VRS:|«MPB»|«MPE»|«MPM»|«MPC»||
||Contained in 20VRS:|«MPB»|«MPE»|«MPM»|«MPC»|«-»|
||Contained in 21VRS:|«MPB»|«-»|«MPM»|«MPC»|«-»|
||Hardware|--|||||
||Funct. package(s):|--|||||
||Device parameter:|axis-specific|||||



> Function This parameter is provided for the (motor-related) load inertia reduced to the motor. It is used for: 

- Automatic control loop setting (C1800) 

- encoderless, flow-controlled motor operation (FXC) 

If none of the above cases is used, it is not necessary to enter a value. De‐ pending on bit 9 of parameter "P-0-4, Motor type", the value has a different meaning: 

- Load inertia, motor-related (without rotor inertia) for rotary motors 

- Load mass (without primary part mass) for linear motors 

See also Functional Description "Automatic setting of axis control" 

Use 

Automatic control loop setting 

The load inertia can be automatically determined by executing the command "P-0-0162, C1800 Command Drive optimization / command value box". If the axis-side inertia value is exactly known, then this value should be entered in P-0-4010. The load inertia or load mass is essential for optimizing the velocity control loop. 

Encoderless, flow-controlled motor operation (FXC) 

In sensorless, flux-controlled motor operation, the value of the motor-related load inertia is essential for setting the frequency controller. Therefore, the motor-related axis-side inertia value has to be entered. The value may be available from the machine design, otherwise it has to be determined by a run-up test. 

See also the functional description "Sensorless motor operation, flow-control‐ led" 

Automatic control loop adjustment (C1800) and encoderless, fluxcontrolled motor operation are mutually exclusive!

This parameter contains a percent value which is referring to parameter "S-0-0109, Motor peak current" for synchronous motors. If this percentage value is multiplied with the value of "S-0-0109", the result is the current limit value. If the electric current limit value is exceeded, the magnets of the syn‐ chronous motor risk being permanently demagnetized. 

In case the limit value is exceeded, the power output stage of the controller is temporarily disabled to protect the motor, until the electric current has fallen below the limit value again. Warning E8028 is generated in the disabled state. 

The correct value is written to this parameter as follows: 

- In case of Rexroth motors with encoder data memory: Automatic when controller is switched on. 

- In case of Rexroth motors without encoder data memory: 

   - By loading the motor parameters with commissioning soft‐ ware "IndraWorks Ds/D/MLD". 

- In case of other motors: 

   - By manual input according to the manufacturer's specifica‐ tion. 

See also functional description "Limitations"

Bosch Rexroth AG R911328651_Edition 15 

IndraDrive MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB Parameters 

1163/1717 

Product-specific parameters 

For some parameters it is necessary that the drive firmware adjusts the units and decimal places to the type of construction of the motor (rotary or linear). In this case, the respective units and decimal places are specified directly for the concerned parameter. 

## Motors with encoder data memory 

In the case of Rexroth motors with encoder data memory, the bits of this pa‐ rameter are automatically set correctly! This is done during boot-up (after switching on the controller) and with every transition to phase 4 (ready for op‐ eration state). 

Motors without encoder data memory 

In the case of Rexroth motors without encoder data memory, the bits of this parameter are automatically set correctly when the motor parameters are loa‐ ded from the database of the "IndraWorks Ds/D/MLD" commissioning soft‐ ware. 

## Third-party motors 

If the characteristic of the quadrature-axis inductance of the motor is speci‐ fied for synchronous third-party motors (manufacturer data for "P-0-4002" and "P-0-4003"), the following applies with regard to bit 12 and bit 11: 

- Any reluctance property cannot be used for synchronous third-party mo‐ tors! Determining motor parameter values which are safe to operate for using the reluctance property is impossible for third-party motors, for which reason bit 11 may not be set. 

- If, due to lacking bandwidth in the current control loop, the drive tends to oscillation when the velocity controller is set or optimized, bit 12 should be set to "1" by way of trial. If there is no improvement, reset the bit.

Function 

For synchronous motors, the direct-axis inductance of the motor is entered in this parameter. The direct-axis inductance is the inductance of the d-axis in the field-oriented d-q coordinate system and is also called Ld. Observe that for the direct-axis inductance of the motor a value is expected that was deter‐ mined from the inductances of the 3-phase motor model by space vector transformation.

## 4.18.272 P-0-4018, Positioning block delay time 

Allocation Contained in 16VRS: «MPB» «MPE» «MPM» Contained in 17VRS: «MPB» «MPE» «MPM» «MPC» Contained in 18VRS: «MPB» «MPE» «MPM» «MPC» Contained in 20VRS: «MPB» «MPE» «MPM» «MPC» «-» Contained in 21VRS: «MPB» «-» «MPM» «MPC» «-» Hardware -- Funct. package(s): CL Device parameter: axis-specific 

> Function In the positioning block mode, parameter P-0-4018 is used to parameterize a defined delay time between the individual positioning blocks. 

See also Functional Description "Positioning Block Mode" 

> Use As this is a list parameter with 64 elements, you can define individual and dif‐ ferent delay times at block transition for all 64 positioning blocks. 

Observe the following aspects for parameterization: 

● The positioning block mode delay time only takes effect for a sequential block with intermediate stop. 

- When the programmed target position of the block has been reached, the drive waits for the delay time P-0-4018[n] until the sequential block block[n+1] is started.

## 4.18.278 P-0-4025, Drive address of the master communication 

Allocation 

Contained in 16VRS: «MPB» «MPE» «MPM» Hardware -- -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: axis-specific 

> Function By means of this parameter, the address for master communication (e.g., SERCOS, Profibus…) can be set. 

The effective address can be taken either directly from "S-0-0096, Slave arrangement (SLKN)" or from "P-0-4031, Overview of de‐ vice addresses"! 

See also Functional Description "Serial Communication" 

> Use Observe the following aspects for parameterization: 

R911328651_Edition 15 Bosch Rexroth AG 

IndraDrive MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB Parameters 

1168/1717 

Product-specific parameters 

- The parameter can be set via the control panel, the serial interface or the master communication interface. 

With SERCOS, it can only be changed in phase 0, with all other devices in the parameter mode ("PM"). 

- The entered address does not take immediate effect, but: 

   - SERCOS: Only at the next change of communication phase from "phase 0" to "phase 1" might it therefore be necessary to run up the drive again 

   - Field bus and analog/parallel: at the next change to the operating mode ("OM") 

- With the setting "P-0-4022" = "256" (default value), the address set in "P-0-4025, Drive address of master communication" is used for serial communication. 

See also Parameter Description "P-0-4031, Overview of device addresses" 

See also Parameter Description "S-0-0096, Slave arrangement (SLKN)"

> Function This parameter can be used to deactivate the hardware of an axis of a multiaxis device, i.e. the hardware of an axis (output stage, etc.) is not available for the firmware. This reduces the number of present axes of a multi-axis de‐ vice. 

As a result, the assignment of the firmware axis to the hardware axis may change. If the hardware of the second axis is deactivated, there will be the following axis assignment of firmware to existing hardware: 

|<br>Function|Firmware axis|Hardware axis|
|---|---|---|
||1|1|
||2|3|
||3|4|
||(4)||
||Tab. 4-344:<br>Assignment of Firmware Axis to Hardware Axis||



If an axis is to be deactivated or reactivated via this parameter, the device must be switched off and on again or "S01350, C6400 reboot command" must be executed after a value has been writ‐ ten to the parameter. Thereafter, the parameters of the existing axes are invalid. As a result, the existing axes must be re-para‐ meterized. 

The default setting is activation of all existing axes of a device. At least one axis of a device must remain active.

## 4.18.285 P-0-4032, Motor type plate data

1173/1717 

Product-specific parameters 

## Function 

For asynchronous third-party motors it is possible via "C3200 Command Cal‐ culate motor data" to calculate the values for motor parameters from the type plate data and then the values of the motor control parameters. 

With FW 20VRS and above, "C3200 Command Calculate motor data" can also be used for rotary synchronous third-party motors. 

The activation of C3200 first requires manual input of the motor data from the type plate of the motor in list parameter "P-0-4032, Motor type plate data". 

If a Rexroth motor is used, the content of "P-0-4032" and the command C3200 are irrelevant as for these motors all parameters required for operation are stored in the database for motor data (Drive Base). 

See also Functional Description "Automatic setting of motor control" 

## Structure 

The individual list elements have the following function: 

|List ele‐<br>ment|Motor variable|Default<br>value|Unit|Definition|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|0|Rated current|4.000|Arms|Effective value of the electrical<br>current in motor supply (motor<br>phase) at rated load|
|1|Rated voltage<br>(asynchronous mo‐<br>tor only)|380.000|Vrms|Effective value of interlinked<br>voltage between motor connec‐<br>tion terminals at rated load|
|2|Rated frequency|50.000|Hz|Frequency of supply, sine, elec‐<br>tric voltage|
|3|Rated speed|925.000|rpm|Speed of the motor output shaft<br>at rated load|
|4|Power factor cos φ<br>(asynchronous mo‐<br>tor only)|0.760|1|Power factor at rated load|
|5|Rated power|1.500|kW|permanent mechanical power<br>output at rated load|



Tab. 4-347: List elements P-0-4032 

Rated load means load of the motor output shaft with the rated torque at supply of the motor with rated voltage and rated fre‐ quency. The rated load point has to not be within the field weak‐ ening range. The power at the output shaft is the rated power. 

## Use 

Observe the following for parameterization or element input: 

- All specifications in "P-0-4032" must describe the same working point of the motor. This working point must not inside the field weakening range and should describe S1 operation (continuous power of the motor). 

- All list elements are 32-bit values and have 3 decimal places. 

- The list parameter has a fixed length of 6 elements. 

- The parameter can only be written in CM and PM. 

R911328651_Edition 15 Bosch Rexroth AG

1174/1717 

Product-specific parameters 

- The data in "P-0-4032" do not have a direct influence on motor control. Not before starting command C3200 via "P-0-4033", all motor data (T equivalent diagram) and motor control parameters are calculated.
