## 5.5.99 S-0-1305.0.1, System time 

|Allocation|Contained in 20VRS:|«MPB»|«MPE»|«MPM»|«MPC»|«PSB»|
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
||Contained in 21VRS:|«MPB»|«-»|«MPM»|«MPC»|«PSB»|
||Hardware|--|||||
||Funct. package(s):|--|||||
||Device parameter:|device-specific|||||



> Function This 8-byte parameter contains the system time in the IEC 61588 format. 

It is composed of the 4-byte individual parameters "S-0-1305.0.2, System time (fine)" and "S-0-1305.0.3, System time (coarse)". The lower 4 bytes con‐ tain the nanoseconds part (up to 999999999), and the upper 4 bytes the sec‐ onds part of the system time starting from 01/01/1970. 

The content of this parameter is updated with each position acquisition. This corresponds to updating in the velocity controller clock cycle. When the de‐ vice is switched off, the system time is stored in a non-volatile memory. Upon restarting, updating is continued at the switch-off time. If, while restarting, it is detected that the system time in the retain data memory is invalid, the time is initialized using the date 01/01/2014 (= 1,388,534,400 seconds). 

The system time can be changed with the help of this parameter. A time is accepted with the next position acquisition. 

The system time cannot be changed by means of this parameter, if the sys‐ tem time is cyclically transmitted via a sercos master communication. In this 

Bosch Rexroth AG R911328651_Edition 15 

IndraDrive MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB Parameters 

1565/1717 Standard parameters 

case, the system time in the slave is cyclically compared to that received from the master. Deviations up to 5 µs are ignored. If the deviation exceeds this threshold, the time is corrected in the slave. 

With EtherCAT master communication, the slave can only receive the fine proportion of a cyclically transmitted system time and use it for synchroniza‐ tion. A coarse setting has to be made via the non-cyclic data channel. 

If the system time in the slave is changed by more than 60 seconds, an entry is made in the Diagnostic Trace. In list "S-0-1303.0.12, Diagnostic trace buf‐ fer no3", this is indicated by value 0x000D7FFF. 

In the Advanced device with sercos master the system time is transmitted to connected CCD slaves as cyclic communication starts.

The fine proportion of the system time contained in this parameter is up to one second. The LSB (least significant bit) corresponds to a nanosecond. 

The parameter maps the nanosecond hardware counter, which is latched with each position sensing cycle. 

A write access to this parameter results in a change in the system time. At the same time, any value written to parameter S-0-1305.0.3 before for the coarse proportion is also accepted. The time is accepted with the next posi‐ tion sensing cycle.

> Function This command is used to activate a drive restart. 

While the command is executed, the parameters to be saved are stored. Af‐ ter a delay of two seconds, the drive is restarted. 

See also Functional Description "SERCOS Interface" 

The reboot command causes the drive firmware to jump to the boot kernel. Execution of the command has the same effect as activation and deactivation of the 24-V supply. This may result in errors on the module bus or in the master communication of neighboring drives. 

> Use The drive firmware comprises activities after which the drive must be switch‐ ed off and on. This can be achieved with the reboot command. 

A reboot command can be executed after the following activities: 

- Function package switching 

- Change of the master communication protocol 

- Firmware download

## 5.6.39 S-0-1703.0.155, Mains synchronization, control word 

Allocation Contained in 21VRS: «PSB» Hardware Power supply -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: device-specific 

> Function This control word can be used to influence the behavior of the grid synchroni‐ zation in the event of events in the supply or integrated grid. 

> Structure The following bits are included in the control word. 

Use 

|Bit|Designation/function|Comment|
|---|---|---|
|0|Activation of dynamic network support according to VDE-<br>AR-N 4110<br>0:Not active/no FRT<br>1:Active /FRT||
|Tab. 5-117:<br>S‑0‑1703.0.155|||
|Changes in the control word need to be made only in special ope‐<br>rating cases. Always use default values for normal operation at<br>the mains.|||



Bit 0: If the controller is used as part of a power generation system on the mains in accordance with VDE-AR-N 4110, FRT (Fault Ride Through) opera‐ tion can be activated at the time of the mains voltage dip. This allows the volt‐ age dip to be passed without mains voltage error messages.

## 5.6.40 S-0-1703.0.156, Synchronization of negative sequence P-gain 

Allocation Contained in 21VRS: «PSB» Hardware Power supply -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: device-specific 

> Function The parameter can be used to adjust the dynamics of the synchronization controller for the counter system. 

> Use The parameter is only to be used if the device is operated as part of a power generation system in accordance with VDE-AR-N 4110 and a reactive current injection into the negative sequence component is intended in the course of dynamic network support. The parameter is only effective when the negative sequence current controller (S-0-1709.0.150 Current controller, control word, bit 13) is active and a minimum voltage is present in the negative sequence component. 

By default, the synchronization controller is preconfigured with a gain of 1, with a good balance between dynamics and robustness. Higher values in‐ crease the dynamics and lower values increase the robustness. The dynamic behavior of the synchronization controller can be analyzed by means of a step change of the voltage in the negative sequence compnent with the help of the two voltage components d and q.

## 5.6.43 S-0-1703.0.172, Phase failure, threshold 3 

Contained in 21VRS: «PSB» Hardware Power supply -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: device-specific 

Allocation 

Function 

The phase failure threshold defines at which phase deviation of the mains voltage the device detects a phase failure and outputs the diagnostics E2818 or F2818. Phase monitoring is performed in three stages. The third level or threshold can be set via this parameter. 

Use 

During normal operation on the mains, the default value should be main‐ tained for correct operation of the device. If the device is part of a power gen‐ eration system according to VDE-AR-N 4110 and the operating mode dynam‐ ic grid support is required, the phase failure threshold can be lowered.

1585/1717 

Standard parameters 

> Function Input parameters for the active current command value in "Current Control" mode. The parameter can be specified cyclically. 

> Use The value entered in the parameter is applied by the voltage control cyclical‐ ly, limited by "S-0-1708.0.13" and filtered with the time constant entered in parameter "S-0-1708.0.150". 

If an active current-generating command value is specified, the power supply generates a current whose phase is equal to the measured supply voltage. A positive active current runs from the power supply to the mains. 

This parameter is only effective in "Current Control" mode.

## 5.6.47 S-0-1706.0.12, Reactive-current generating component, command value 

Allocation Contained in 20VRS: «PSB» Contained in 21VRS: «PSB» Hardware -- -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: device-specific Alias: P-0-0874 

> Function Input parameters for the reactive current command value in "Current Control" mode and for active DC bus voltage control if no reactive power control is ac‐ tive. The parameter can be specified cyclically. 

> Use The value entered in this parameter is applied and limited by the current con‐ trol cyclically. With active limiting, active current takes precedence over reac‐ tive current. 

If a reactive current-generating command value is specified, the power supply generates a current whose phase differs from the measured supply voltage by 90°. A positive reactive current runs from the power supply to the mains and results in capacitative be‐ havior. 

This parameter is effective in "Current Control" mode and for active DC bus voltage control if no reactive power control is active. 

See also Functional Description "Current Control" 

See also Functional Description "Reactive Power Control"

> Function This parameter is used to specify the target command value for the infeeding mode in the "voltage control, floating DC bus voltage" mode. The parameter can be cyclically written. 

> Use The value entered in the parameter is cyclically applied by the DC bus volt‐ age control. However, the parameter is only taken into account in the "volt‐ age control, floating DC bus voltage" mode. 

If the DC bus voltage drops below the actual value from "S-0-1708.0.152, Lower DC bus voltage threshold", DC bus voltage control is activated until the entered command value has been reached. Afterwards, DC bus voltage control is deactivated. 

Observe the following rule for entering the value: 

Internal lower limit < S-0-1708.0.152 < S-0-1706.0.152 < S-0-1706.0.153 < S-0-1708.0.153 < internal maximum value

## 5.6.60 S-0-1707.0.160, Reactive power, actual value 

Allocation Contained in 20VRS: «PSB» Contained in 21VRS: «PSB» Hardware -- -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: device-specific Alias: P-0-2733 

Function 

Use 

This parameter displays the current reactive power. 

It only displays an actual reactive power value when the reactive power con‐ trol "S-0-1709.0.160 Reactive power controller" is active in "Voltage Control" mode. 

The actual reactive power value is comprised of the configured power supply reactive power and the mains connection reactive power (mains filter and mains choke). If the mains connection is excluded via parameter "S-0-1709.0.160, Reactive power controller", the actual reactive power value consists only of the power supply reactive power. The reactive power of the mains connection is not included. 

If a positive reactive power is determined, the power supply is in‐ ductive. 

See also Functional Description "Reactive Power Control"

## 5.6.66 S-0-1708.0.1, DC bus voltage controller proportional gain 

R911328651_Edition 15 Bosch Rexroth AG 

IndraDrive MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB Parameters 

1594/1717 

Standard parameters 

> Function The DC bus voltage controller forms an active current-generating supply cur‐ rent command value (S-0-1707.0.11) from the difference between the DC bus voltage command value and the DC bus voltage. 

See also Functional Description "DC Bus Voltage Control" 

> Use The active current-generating command value component consists of: 

- Proportional part: 

P = S-0-1708.0.1 x (S-0-1706.0.1 - S-0-1707.0.1) 

   - Active current-generating command value component (proportional part) 

- Integral part 

I = t x S-0-1708.0.1 ÷ S-0-1708.0.2 x (S-0-1706.0.1 - S-0-1707.0.1) 

   - Active current-generating command value component (integral part) 

- This results in the following transfer function for the PI controller: S-0-1707.0.11(t) = S-0-1708.0.1 x (1 + t ÷ S-0-1708.0.2) x (S-0-1706.0.1 - S-0-1707.0.1) 

Transfer function for the PI controller 

The "C0710 Load defaults procedure (motor-specific controller values)" com‐ mand makes it possible to load a default value for this parameter.

## 5.6.67 S-0-1708.0.2, DC bus voltage controller integral action time 

Allocation Contained in 20VRS: «PSB» Contained in 21VRS: «PSB» Hardware -- -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: device-specific Alias: P-0-0802 

> Function The DC bus voltage controller forms an active current-generating mains cur‐ rent command value (S-0-1707.0.11) from the difference between the DC bus voltage command value and the actual DC bus voltage value. 

See also Functional Description "DC bus voltage control" 

Use 

The active current-generating command value component consists of: 

- Proportional term: 

P-term = S-0-1708.0.1 * (S-0-1706.0.1 - S-0-1707.0.1) 

Active current-generating command value component (proportional term) 

- Integral term: 

I-term = t * S-0-1708.0.1/S-0-1708.0.2 * (S-0-1706.0.1 - S-0-1707.0.1) 

Active current-generating command value component (integral term) 

- This results in the following transfer function for the PI controller: 

   - S-0-1707.0.11(t) = S-0-1708.0.1 * (1 + t/S-0-1708.0.2) * (S-0-1706.0.1 - S-0-1707.0.1) 

The "C0710 Load defaults procedure (power-supply specific controller val‐ ues)" command allows a default value to be loaded for this parameter. 

Defining the integral action time 

Bosch Rexroth AG R911328651_Edition 15 

IndraDrive MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB Parameters 

1595/1717 

Standard parameters 

"S-0-1708.0.2, Integral action time" refers to the value on the time axis where the integral term equals the proportional term. It means the time a purely integral controller would need until the controller output variable y equals the output variable of a propor‐ tional controller when time t = 0.

## 5.6.68 S-0-1708.0.11, Mains current controller proportional gain 

Allocation 

Function 

Use 

Contained in 20VRS: «PSB» Contained in 21VRS: «PSB» Hardware -- -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: device-specific Alias: P-0-0800 

This parameter defines the proportional gain for the current controller (Id and Iq control loop). The parameterization of the current controller proportional gain depends on the inductance of the commutation choke, on the control performance (current controller clock TA,i) and on the switching frequency (S-0-1709.0.151). 

The "C0710 Load defaults procedure (motor-specific controller values)" com‐ mand makes it possible to load a default value for this parameter. The induc‐ tance of the commutation choke, the active performance and the active switching frequency (S-0-1709.0.151) are included here. It is therefore typi‐ cally unnecessary to adjust the determined proportional gain.

## 5.6.76 S-0-1708.0.152, Lower DC bus voltage threshold 

Allocation Contained in 20VRS: «PSB» Contained in 21VRS: «PSB» Hardware -- -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: device-specific Alias: P-0-2706 

> Function This parameter is used to specify the lower DC bus voltage threshold in the "voltage control, floating DC bus voltage" mode. The parameter can be cycli‐ cally written. 

See also Functional Description "Voltage control, floating DC bus voltage" 

> Use The value entered in the parameter is cyclically applied by the DC bus volt‐ age control. However, the parameter is only taken into account in the "volt‐ age control, floating DC bus voltage" mode. 

If the DC bus voltage drops below the entered actual value, DC bus voltage control is activated with the command value from "S-0-1706.0.152, DC bus voltage command value, feeding".

Internal lower limit < S-0-1708.0.152 < S-0-1706.0.152 < S-0-1706.0.153 < S-0-1708.0.153 < internal maximum value

## 5.6.80 S-0-1708.0.170, Negative sequence current controller proportional gain 

Allocation Contained in 21VRS: «PSB» Hardware -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: device-specific Alias: P-0-3876 Function The negative sequence current controller forms the proportional part of the manipulated variable from S-0-1707.0.193 (or S-0-1707.0.192) from the dif‐ ference between S-0-1706.0.191 and S-0-1707.0.191 (or S-0-1707.0.190) via the entered amplification factor. Use The parameter is only to be used if the device is operated as part of a power generation system in accordance with VDE-AR-N 4110 and a reactive current injection into the negative sequence component is required in the course of dynamic network support. The parameter is only effective when the negative sequence current controller is active (S-0-1709.0.150 Current controller, con‐ trol word, bit 13). 

The proportional gain determines the level of the additive setpoint current when there is a control difference for the positive sequence component. A high gain factor increases the dynamic response of the transient oscillation process. Too high a value can lead to oscillating behavior. It is recommended to choose a smaller gain factor and thus a lower dynamic range in order to increase the system stability.

## 5.6.82 S-0-1709.0.1, Primary operation mode 

Allocation Contained in 20VRS: «PSB» Contained in 21VRS: «PSB» Hardware -- -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: device-specific 

> Function This input parameter can be used to preselect an operating mode from the list of supported operating modes (S-0-1705.0.1). The operation modes are controlled in all communication buses by using the control word of the supply unit (S-0-1720.0.1). 

The operation mode determined in this parameter is activated in the drive if: 

- The primary operation mode is selected in the control word 

- control and power sections are ready for operation 

- drive enable "RF" was set 

See also Functional Description "Selecting the operation mode" 

> Use The operation mode is set by entering a binary value. Possible operation modes are: 

- Voltage control (stable DC bus voltage with command value) 

- Rectifier mode, load-dependent (rectifier mode with command value as regenerative threshold or command value at high currents) 

- Current control (constant mains current control with current command values Iq and Id)

## 5.6.91 S-0-1710.0.2, Thermal device load 

> Function Parameter "S-0-1710.0.2" is used to check the thermal load of the amplifier. 0% corresponds to a chip overtemperature of 0 K. 100% corresponds to the maximum chip overtemperature. If the power supply is designed properly, the thermal load should not exceed 80% for the specified machining cycles. 

> Use The typical duration for heating a control unit power output stage to final tem‐ perature is approx. 10 mins. The control unit load can be preset to 80% in or‐ der to check the thermal power supply load during start-up without having to perform machining cycles within this period. This can be done by writing the parameter "S-0-1710.0.2". 

- Due to the switching loss of the power supply, "S-0-1710.0.2" always shows a value > 0 when control is enabled, even if the current equals 0. 

- Amplifier current is limited when the load reaches approx. 97%. This is displayed with the warning "E8057 Amplifier overload, current limit ac‐ tive".

## 5.6.107 S-0-1712.0.190, Active power-dependent cos(phi) characteristic: performance 

Allocation 

Function 

Contained in 20VRS: «PSB» Contained in 21VRS: «PSB» Hardware -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: device-specific 

This parameter defines the active power axis for the cos(φ) characteristic. The cos(φ) axis is given by "S-0-1712.0.191". Using the characteristic, it is possible to achieve active power-dependent reactive power generation or an active power-dependent power factor. 

The parameter is only active if bit 3 has been set in "S-0-1712.0.150". 

R911328651_Edition 15 Bosch Rexroth AG 

IndraDrive MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB Parameters 

1614/1717 

Standard parameters 

See also Functional Description "Reactive power command value input de‐ pending on the active power" 

> Use At least two list values have to be input. The number of list values has to comply with the one in "S-0-1712.0.191". 

Positive active power flows from the power grid or grid system to the supply unit. The active power values have to be entered in equidistant form. 

The active power values have to be entered as normalized to the device’s nominal active power ("S-0-1712.0.192, Nominal active power of power plant"). The nominal active power of the generating plant can be the nominal active power of the device at the max. That is why the nominal device active power is used as default value for "S-0-1712.0.192, Nominal active power of power plant". If the nominal active power of the power plant is smaller than the nominal active power of the device, "S-0-1712.0.192, Nominal active power of power plant" has to be adjusted accordingly.

## 5.6.113 S-0-1714.0.140, Mains supply version 

Allocation Contained in 21VRS: «PSB» Hardware -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: device-specific 

> Function The parameter shows the version of the firmware component mains supply. 

> Use Display parameters for the version of the mains supply function which in‐ cludes the following functions: 

- Frequency-dependent limitation and reduction of the active power flow to the grid 

- Limiting the active power flow to the mains 

- Reactive power command value input depending on the active power 

- Advanced mains monitoring 

- Dynamic grid support (only support the negative sequence component and prevent grid disconnection in FRT case) 

The version can be used as a basis for the certification of components/ systems, e.g. according to VDE-AR-N 4110, using the supply unit. The ver‐ sion maps the implementation status of the firmware and is used to assess changes to the firmware with regard to the electrical behavior at the grid con‐ nection point during the network supply.

> Use Bit 0-3: The operating mode of the device is set. Depending on the activated operating mode, interconnection of components may need to be adjusted. For activation of the DC/DC converter, the device must be restarted. In pa‐ rameter "S-0-1717.0.151", the currently effective operating mode is dis‐ played. 

Bit 4-7: Definition of the location of mains voltage measurement in island grid mode. This defines the possible island grid modes and whether dynamic op‐ eration mode change is admissible. 

Bit 8: Enables dynamic operation mode change between mains operation and island grid mode. This enables dynamic change from passive mains con‐ sumer (e.g. control of DC bus voltage or mains current) to active mains gen‐ erator.

## 5.6.123 S-0-1716.0.150, Island grid mode control word 

Allocation 

Contained in 21VRS: «PSB» Hardware -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: device-specific Alias: P-0-3863 

> Function With this parameter, island grid mode can be parameterized. 

Structure 

The following settings are possible. 

|Bit|Designation/function|Comment|
|---|---|---|
|0|Characteristic curve mode<br>0:Active<br>1:Not active||
|1|External synchronization<br>0:Not active<br>1:Active<br>Prerequisite:Characteristic curve mode not active||
|2|Current offset compensation<br>0:Not active<br>1:Active||



Tab. 5-127: S‑0‑1716.0.150, Island grid mode control word 

See also function description "Island grid mode" 

> Use The characteristic curve mode to be activated via "bit 0" enables synchroni‐ zation of multiple island grid sources in one grid. By means of parameteriza‐ tion of the characteristic, the working point of the individual sources can be set. Before deactivation of characteristic curve mode at island grids with mul‐ tiple sources, the sequence has to be checked for load distribution. 

By means of external synchronization to be activated via "bit 1", alignment of two grids is possible. For this purpose, voltage and phase controllers are acti‐ vated for adjustment to zero of the voltage and phase differences determined by an external measuring device. 

A DC offset can be compensated in the phase current via "bit 2". A DC offset in the phase currents can result in saturation of a connected, unloaded or lightly loaded transformer. This can result in current harmonics or oscillations with high amplitudes. This becomes evident by the flow of the currents. How‐ ever, partially also by unpleasant noises.

## 5.6.126 S-0-1716.0.162, Island grid voltage, maximum value 

Allocation Contained in 21VRS: «PSB» Hardware -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: device-specific Function Parameter for limitation of the output voltage in island grid mode. 

> Use The parameter is used to protect the AC consumers connected in particularly critical operating cases or for incorrect parameterization of the control. The parameter has no limiting effect on the output voltage in normal operation. 

The controller output of the voltage controller is limited in controlled operation and the specified island grid voltage is limited in regulated operation. 

Due to the voltage drops at the output stage, the value is to be parameterized approx. 20 V below the voltage critical for the AC consumer. 

See also function description "Island grid mode"

## 5.6.131 S-0-1716.0.180, Voltage controller proportional gain 

Allocation Contained in 21VRS: «PSB» Hardware -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: device-specific 

> Function The voltage controller for island grid mode controls the island grid voltage feedback value to the effective island grid voltage command value. For this purpose, a classical PI controller with proportional gain for adjustment by means of this parameter is applied. 

See also function description "Island grid mode" 

> Use Proportional gain defines the level of the voltage controller output for the ex‐ isting control difference. A high gain factor increases the dynamic response of the transient oscillation process. If the value is too high, this may lead to an instable behavior or high overshooting.

## 5.6.134 S-0-1716.0.184, Phase controller proportional gain 

Allocation 

Contained in 21VRS: «PSB» Hardware -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: device-specific 

> Function The phase controller for island grid mode enables control of an existing phase offset between two mains phases and synchronization of two mains. For this purpose, a classical PI controller with proportional gain for adjust‐ ment by means of this parameter is applied. 

See also function description "Island grid mode" 

> Use Proportional gain defines the level of the frequency controller output for the existing control difference. A high gain factor increases the dynamic response of the transient oscillation process. If the value is too high, this may lead to an instable behavior. A lower gain factor and reduced dynamics are recommen‐ ded to minimize the risk of instability. Practical examinations have shown that low dynamic response is also sufficient for quick synchronization.

## 5.6.135 S-0-1716.0.185, Phase controller integral action time 

Allocation Contained in 21VRS: «PSB» Hardware -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: device-specific 

> Function The phase controller for island grid mode enables control of an existing phase offset between two mains phases and synchronization of two mains. For this purpose, a classical PI controller with integral action time for adjust‐ ment by means of this parameter is applied. 

See also function description "Island grid mode" 

> Use The integral action time influences the time period in which the control differ‐ ence is eliminated. A short reset time increases the dynamics of the transient response. If the value is too low, this may lead to an instable behavior. Practi‐ cal examinations have shown that a pure P controller is often sufficient. The I-term has to be deactivated upon commissioning start. This is possible by re‐ setting the integral action time to zero.

## 5.6.142 S-0-1717.0.150, Island grid mode status word 

Allocation 

Function 

Structure 

Contained in 21VRS: «PSB» Hardware -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: device-specific Alias: P-0-3809 

This parameter enables reading out of status information of island grid mode. See also function description "Island grid mode" 

The following status information is provided. 

|Bit|Designation/function|Comment|
|---|---|---|
|0|Island grid analysis result during Bb operating phase<br>0:Island grid voltage-free<br>1:Island grid not zero potential||
|1|Synchronization to grid<br>0:Not synchronized<br>1:Synchronized||
|2|External synchronization<br>0:Not synchronized<br>1:Synchronized||



Tab. 5-128: Island grid mode status word 

Bit 0: Indicates whether a voltage was recognized during analysis of the is‐ land grid in the Bb operating phase. This is required to distinguish between the operating cases "Black start" from "Synchronization with existing island grid". The condition for this, however, is connection of mains voltage meas‐ urement between consumer/load and main contactor. 

Bits 2/1: In the case of a synchronization, they indicate whether it has been completed. In this process, it is checked whether the control difference of an‐ gle and voltage controller has fallen below an internally defined threshold.

## 5.6.144 S-0-1718.0.160, External synchronization, voltage difference 

Allocation Contained in 21VRS: «PSB» Hardware -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: device-specific Alias: P-0-3810 

> Function If the island grid in place is to be synchronized with another grid, the grid dif‐ ferences have to be determined via an external measuring point. If the devia‐ tions of the other grid from the island grid are known, they may be adjusted. Via this parameter, the voltage difference of both grids is transmitted (in V, current values of external conductor as reference). 

A command value minus the actual value is expected. This means, target voltage minus the voltage of the island grid system. 

See also function description "Island grid mode"

## 5.6.150 S-0-1731.0.22, Equivalent capacitance of mains connection 

Allocation Contained in 20VRS: «PSB» Contained in 21VRS: «PSB» Hardware -- -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: device-specific 

> Function Input parameter for the equivalent capacitance of the mains connection. 

> Use This parameter is required as the basis for determining the reactive power of the mains connection. The capacitance acting toward the neutral point be‐ tween mains connection and pre-choke/commutation choke must be entered in this parameter if no pre-choke is used. Capacitance is usually determined from the capacitance of the mains filter and, if necessary, the pre-capaci‐ tance of the mains choke if no pre-choke is used. 

If the capacitors are in a delta connection, a conversion must be made to a wye connection (C_Wye = 3 x C_Delta). 

The input value always represents the total capacitance between a phase and the neutral point. If there are multiple capacitor connections, the total ca‐ pacitance must be determined.

## 5.6.158 S-0-1741.0.171, DC voltage controller proportional gain 

Allocation 

Contained in 21VRS: «PSB» Hardware -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: device-specific Alias: P-0-1649 

> Function The DC voltage controller forms a DC command value from the difference between DC voltage command value and DC voltage actual value. 

See also Functional Description "Operation modes" 

> Use This DC command value consists of: 

- A proportional term: 

P-term = S-0-1741.0.171 * (S-0-1741.0.160 - S-0-1742.0.160) Current command value (proportional term) 

- An integral term: 

I-term = t * S-0-1741.0.171/S-0-1741.0.172 * (S-0-1741.0.160 - S-0-1742.0.160) 

Current command value (integral term) 

- This results in the following transfer function for the PI controller: S-0-1742.0.162(t) = S-0-1741.0.171 * (1 + t/S-0-1741.0.172) * (S-0-1741.0.160 - S-0-1742.0.160) 

It is recommended to design the PI controller according to the symmetric opti‐ mum. The proportional gain is calculated according to the following formula: Kp = 1/α*CDC/TSum_u 

Kp: Proportional gain 

α: Damping factor 

CDC: DC capacity at the output side of the DC/DC converter 

TSum_u: Sum time constant of the DC voltage control circuit 

A value of ≥ 4 is recommended for the damping factor. The sum time con‐ stant consists of half the current controller cycle time, half the PWM periodic time and half the voltage controller cycle time. 

Additionally, the current command value filter must be taken into account, if active (S-0-1741.0.183). 

If the DC voltage command value is read in via an external measuring unit and an analog input, the following aspects will be added as well: 

- Filter behavior or deceleration behavior of the external measuring unit, if applicable 

Bosch Rexroth AG R911328651_Edition 15 

IndraDrive MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB Parameters 

1639/1717 

Standard parameters 

- Time constant for the analog input filter, if the filter is activated

## 5.6.159 S-0-1741.0.172, DC voltage controller integral action time 

Allocation 

Contained in 21VRS: «PSB» Hardware -- Funct. package(s): Device parameter: device-specific Alias: P-0-1650 

> Function The DC voltage controller forms a DC command value from the difference between DC voltage command value and DC voltage actual value. See also Functional Description "Operation modes" 

> Use This DC command value consists of: ● A proportional term: 

P-term = S-0-1741.0.171 * (S-0-1741.0.160 - S-0-1742.0.160) Current command value (proportional term) ● An integral term: 

I-term = t * S-0-1741.0.171/S-0-1741.0.172 * (S-0-1741.0.160 - S-0-1742.0.160) 

Current command value (integral term) 

- This results in the following transfer function for the PI controller: S-0-1742.0.162(t) = S-0-1741.0.171 * (1 + t/S-0-1741.0.172) * (S-0-1741.0.160 - S-0-1742.0.160) 

Defining the integral action time 

"S-0-1741.0.172, Integral action time" refers to the value on the time axis where the integral term equals the proportional term. It means the time a purely integral controller would need until the controller output variable y equals the output variable of a propor‐ tional controller when time t = 0. 

R911328651_Edition 15 Bosch Rexroth AG 

IndraDrive MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB Parameters 

1640/1717

Fig. 5-46: Explanation of integral action time Tn and proportional gain Kp with PI controller 

The input value "S-0-1741.0.172 = 0 ms" switches off the integral term. 

It is recommended to design the PI controller according to the symmetric opti‐ mum. The integral action time is calculated according to the following formu‐ la: 

Tn = α[2] * TSum_i 

α: Damping factor 

TSum_u: Sum time constant of the DC voltage control circuit 

A value of ≥ 4 is recommended for damping. 

The sum time constant consists of half the current controller cycle time, half the PWM periodic time and 125 µs.

## 5.7.4 S-0-1800.0.10, SSO Device Status 

There are the following states: 

Undefined: Is represented by the value 0 Self-Testing: Is represented by the value 1 Idle: Is represented by the value 2 Self-Test Exception: Is represented by the value 3 Executing: Is represented by the value 4 Abort: Is represented by the value 5 Critical Fault: Is represented by the value 6 Configuring: Is represented by the value 7 

R911328651_Edition 15 Bosch Rexroth AG 

IndraDrive MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB Parameters 

1646/1717 

Standard parameters 

Waiting for TUNID: Is represented by the value 8 

The values from 9 to 50 are reserved by the CIP protocol. The values from 51 to 99 are device-specific. The values from 100 to 255 are manufacturer-spe‐ cific.

> Function The parameter represents the revision number (major and minor) of the CIP identity object. CIP also uses the attribute 4. The minor revision is assigned to the lower octet of the two-byte value, whereas the major revision is as‐ signed to the upper octet. 

The most significant bit is reserved for the compatibility bit. The compatibility bit is always set, since the setting is applied to the SDDML. However, this does not affect the controllability via the Forward Open request.

## 6 Communication Objects (0x1000 to 0x1FFF) 

The communication objects are described in the CANopen standard DS301. Within the CANopen communication, these objects have one of the following functions: 

- Access to drive parameters 

- Constants 

- Read-only objects

1661/1717 Service and support 

## 7 Service and support 

Our worldwide service network provides an optimized and efficient support. Our experts offer you advice and assistance should you have any queries. You can contact us 24/7 . 

## Service Germany 

Our technology-oriented Competence Center in Lohr, Germany, is responsi‐ ble for all your service-related queries for electric drive and controls. 

Contact the Service Hotline and Service Helpdesk under: 

Phone: +49 9352 40 5060 Fax: +49 9352 18 4941 E-mail: service.svc@boschrexroth.de Internet: http://www.boschrexroth.com 

Additional information on service, repair (e.g. delivery addresses) and training can be found on our internet sites. 

Service worldwide 

Preparing information 

Outside Germany, please contact your local service office first. For hotline numbers, refer to the sales office addresses on the internet. 

To be able to help you more quickly and efficiently, please have the following information ready: 

- Detailed description of malfunction and circumstances 

- Type plate specifications of the affected products, in particular type co‐ des and serial numbers 

- Your contact data (phone and fax number as well as your e-mail ad‐ dress)

Explanation of the parameter attributes 

## Explanation of the parameter attributes 

## Comb. check: 

## Combination check 

-- : When a value is written to them, the operating data are not checked for a valid combination (bit lists). 

+ : When a value is written to them, the operating data are checked for a valid combination (bit lists). 

## Cycl. tra.: 

## Cyclically transmittable 

-- : The operating data can not be configured as cyclic data in the master data telegram or in the drive telegram. 

AT : The operating data can be configured as cyclic data in the drive tele‐ gram. 

MDT : The operating data can be configured as cyclic data in the master data telegram. 

AT+MDT : The operating data can be configured as cyclic data in the master data telegram and in the drive telegram. 

## Data length: 

## Data length 

2 bytes : The data length of the operating data is 2 bytes. 

4 bytes : The data length of the operating data is 4 bytes. 

8 bytes : The data length of the operating data is 8 bytes. 

1 byte var : The operating data are of variable length (list). The length of a da‐ ta element is 1 byte. 

2 byte var : The operating data are of variable length (list). The length of a da‐ ta element is 2 bytes. 

4 byte var : The operating data are of variable length (list). The length of a da‐ ta element is 4 bytes. 

8 byte var : The operating data are of variable length (list). The length of a da‐ ta element is 8 bytes. 

## Decim. pl.: 

## Decimal place 

Indicates the number of decimal places with display formats DEC_OV and DEC_MV. 

IndraDrive MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB Parameters 

1664/1717 

Explanation of the parameter attributes 

Example: 6 decimal transmitted value: 30000 ⇒ display value 0.030000. 

places, 

## Default 

## Default value 

The parameter is set to its default value if the "S-0-0262, C07_x Load de‐ faults procedure command" is executed. This is achieved as follows: 

- Push the <ESC> key when the display shows "PL", or 

- Select command "S-0-0262" with "P-0-4090, Configuration for loading de‐ fault values" (factory settings)="1". 

The default value is only relevant for parameters with attribute PARAM_SP or FIX_IDN_SP Deviating "configurable factory default values" might possibly have been activated. 

## Editable: 

Editability of the operating data: 

-- : Cannot be edited. 

++ : Can always be edited. 

P2 : Can only be edited in communication phase 2. 

P23 : Can be edited in communication phases 2 and 3. 

P3 : Can only be edited in communication phase 3. 

P4 : Can only be edited in communication phase 4. PM : Can only be edited in parameterization mode. OM - Can only be edited in operating mode. 

CCD_P2 - Can only be edited in CCD phase 2. 

SCM - Can only be edited in SMO configuration mode. 

## Extr. val. ch.: 

## Extreme value check 

-- (no) : When a value is written to it, the operating data are not checked for their extreme values. 

+ (yes) : When a value is written to it, the operating data are checked for their extreme values. 

## Format: 

Format of the operating data BIN : Binary number 

IndraDrive MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB Parameters 

1665/1717 

Explanation of the parameter attributes 

HEX : Hexadecimal number 

DEC_OV : Unsigned decimal number DEC_MV : Signed decimal number ASCII : Text IDN : Ident number FLOAT : Floating-point number TIME : Specified time in "sercos time" format 

## Function: 

Par : The parameter is used to display, set and configure values. Cmd : The parameter is used to execute commands. 

## Memory: 

Storage location . This parameter attribute specifies where the parameter is stored. 

-- : The operating data are not buffered in the drive; the value after switching the drive controller on is not defined. 

FIX_IDN_SP : The operating data are stored in the non-volatile memory on the control panel. 

PARAM_SP : The operating data are stored in the non-volatile memory on the control panel. 

ON_BOARD_SP : The operating data are stored in the non-volatile memory on the control section. 

RETAIN_KUNDE : In the event of a control voltage failure, the operating data are stored in the non-volatile memory on the control section. 

RETAIN_GERAET : In the event of a control voltage failure, the operating da‐ ta are stored in the non-volatile memory on the device. 

FEEDBACK, FEEDB_I2C : The operating data are stored in the non-volatile memory of the motor feedback (only in case of Rexroth motors with data feedback). 

LT_SP : The operating data are stored in the non-volatile memory on the pow‐ er section. 

## min./max. 

## Minimum value/maximum value 

The minimum value and maximum value of the parameter are specified de‐ pending on the derivative. 

IndraDrive MPx-16 to MPx-21 and PSB Parameters 

1666/1717 

Explanation of the parameter attributes 

## Set-depend.: 

## Set switchable 

With parameter set switching available, these parameters are available 8 times as a maximum (parameter set 0 to parameter set 7, to parameter set 3 for MPM). 

-- : Available in all parameter sets, not assigned to any parameter group. 

Grp. 1 : The parameter is parameter set switchable, when "group 1, applica‐ tion parameters" has been activated. 

Grp. 2 : The parameter is parameter set switchable, when "group 2, control loop parameters" has been activated. 

Grp. 3 : The parameter is parameter set switchable, when "group 3, load gear parameters" has been activated. 

Grp. 4 : The parameter is parameter set switchable, when "group 4, winding parameters" has been activated. 

Grp. 5 : The parameter is parameter set switchable, when "group 5, motor control and motor encoder 1 parameters" has been activated. 

See also functional description "Parameter set switching" 

## Unit: 

If existing, the corresponding unit of the parameter is specified. 

## Validity ch.: 

## Validity check 

-- : The operating data are not checked for validity. 

P2⇒P3 : The operating data are checked in the command "communication phase 3" transition check. 

P3⇒P4 : The operating data are checked in the command "communication phase 4" transition check. 

PM⇒OM : The operating data are checked in the command "exit parameterization level procedure". 

## Verify: 

Parameters of the integrated safety technology are to be verified during com‐ missioning. The verification ensures that a parameter has been transmitted correctly to the device. 

+ : The parameter value is to be verified during commissioning. 

- : The parameter value does not have to be verified during commissioning.
